title: Recently created customer accounts don't show up using the search feature
need_summary: Whether the customer grid search delay is an intentional indexer behavior or a bug, anchored on the 2.4.8 release notes and commit 1da9ba6f for AC-13810.
security_topic: customer grid indexing and delayed visibility of newly created accounts
question_text: Recently created customer accounts don't show up using the search feature
answer_text:
From the [2.4.8 release notes](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/release/notes/magento-open-source/2-4-8#framework-1):

> Customer Grid indexer does not work properly in Update by Schedule mode

Earlier Customer grid was updated instantly but after the fix Customer grid is updated after cron run but not reflect instantly.

AC-13810 - [GitHub code contribution](https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/1da9ba6f)

@engcom-Bravo I don't think this is an issue

title: Magento installation error: "Current version of RDBMS is not supported" with MariaDB 10.11.14
need_summary: Whether MariaDB 10.11.14 is supported by Magento and which Magento version added support, anchored by commit 9f18dec3e0de2bd5db1fd5c8a03d81e4e80581fd and the Magento 2.4.8-p4 di.xml support matrix.
security_topic: MariaDB version support compatibility for Magento installation
question_text:
Is MariaDB 10.11.14 officially supported by Magento Open Source?
* If not, which MariaDB versions are supported?
* Is there any Magento version compatible with MariaDB 10.11.x?
answer_text:
MariaDB 10.11 support was added in https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/9f18dec3e0de2bd5db1fd5c8a03d81e4e80581fd, these changes were included in Magento 2.4.9-beta1, so the next stable version of Magento: 2.4.9, which is [to be released in 2 weeks](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/release/planning/schedule), will have support for it.

To find out which other MariaDB or MySQL versions are compatible with a certain version of Magento, take a look at this file, and replace the Magento version number in the url to see for which versions support is there: https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p4/app/etc/di.xml#L1876-L1882

title: [Issue] [Bug] GraphQL SearchCriteriaValidator not loaded — removed by module-graph-ql di.xml array override
need_summary: Whether Magento’s GraphQL pageSize validation was being silently dropped by the CompositeValidator array override, with the answer anchored in PR #40742 and the referenced issuecomment confirming the fix.
security_topic: GraphQL pagination validation bypass due to DI array override
question_text: Any GraphQL query with `pageSize` or `currentPage` arguments
answer_text: As per this comment https://github.com/magento/magento2/pull/40742#issuecomment-4419132533 confirming the issue
thread_text:
ISSUE #40762: [Issue] [Bug] GraphQL SearchCriteriaValidator not loaded — removed by module-graph-ql di.xml array override
Author: m2-assistant
Date: 2026-04-21T11:36:13Z
Labels: Issue: Confirmed, Progress: PR Created, Component: GraphQL, Reproduced on 2.4.x, Priority: P3, Progress: done, Reported on 2.4.x, Area: Catalog
State: closed

[c0]
This issue is automatically created based on existing pull request: magento/magento2#40742: [Bug] GraphQL SearchCriteriaValidator not loaded — removed by module-graph-ql di.xml array override

---------
## Preconditions

- Magento 2.4.7-p9 (`magento/module-graph-ql` 100.4.7-p9)
- Any GraphQL query with `pageSize` or `currentPage` arguments

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. Execute any GraphQL query with `pageSize` exceeding the configured limit, e.g.:

```graphql
{
    products(search: "test", pageSize: 999) {
        items {
            sku
        }
    }
}
```

---

## Expected result

GraphQL returns a validation error:

```json
{
    "data": {
        "products": null
    },
    "errors": [
        {
            "message": "Maximum pageSize is 10",
            "path": [
                "products"
            ],
            "locations": [
                {
                    "line": 2,
                    "column": 5
                }
            ],
            "extensions": {
                "category": "graphql-input"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

(`Maximum pageSize is X` — where X is the configured `maxPageSize` value, default 300)

---

## Actual result

Query executes without validation. `pageSize: 999` is accepted silently. No error is returned.

---

## Root cause

`SearchCriteriaValidator` (which enforces `maxPageSize: 300`) is registered
in `magento2-base/app/etc/di.xml` (primary config):

```xml
<!-- magento2-base/app/etc/di.xml -->
<type name="Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="validators" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="searchCriteriaValidator" xsi:type="object">
                Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\SearchCriteriaValidator
            </item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

`module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml` (module config) also defines `validators` for the
same type, but only with `backpressureValidator`:

```xml
<!-- module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml -->
<type name="Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="validators" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="backpressureValidator" xsi:type="object">
                Magento\GraphQl\Model\Backpressure\BackpressureFieldValidator
            </item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

Module-level DI configuration has higher priority than primary config.
When module config defines the same `xsi:type="array"` argument, it **replaces**
the primary config's array — it does **not** merge items. As a result,
`searchCriteriaValidator` is silently dropped.

**Verification at runtime:**

```php
$validator = $objectManager->get(
    \Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator::class
);
$ref = new ReflectionClass($validator);
$prop = $ref->getProperty('validators');
$prop->setAccessible(true);
var_dump(array_keys($prop->getValue($validator)));
// Output: ['backpressureValidator']
// Expected: ['searchCriteriaValidator', 'backpressureValidator']
```

## Proposed fix

Move `searchCriteriaValidator` registration **from** `magento2-base/app/etc/di.xml`
**to** `module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml`. Both validators should live at module level
so that future validators added by third-party modules can safely merge via
`xsi:type="array"`.

### `module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml` — after fix

```xml
<type name="Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="validators" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="searchCriteriaValidator" xsi:type="object">
                Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\SearchCriteriaValidator
            </item>
```

This issue is automatically created based on existing pull request: magento/magento2#40742: [Bug] GraphQL SearchCriteriaValidator not loaded — removed by module-graph-ql di.xml array override

---------
## Preconditions

- Magento 2.4.7-p9 (`magento/module-graph-ql` 100.4.7-p9)
- Any GraphQL query with `pageSize` or `currentPage` arguments

---

## Steps to reproduce

1. Execute any GraphQL query with `pageSize` exceeding the configured limit, e.g.:

```graphql
{
    products(search: "test", pageSize: 999) {
        items {
            sku
        }
    }
}
```

---

## Expected result

GraphQL returns a validation error:

```json
{
    "data": {
        "products": null
    },
    "errors": [
        {
            "message": "Maximum pageSize is 10",
            "path": [
                "products"
            ],
            "locations": [
                {
                    "line": 2,
                    "column": 5
                }
            ],
            "extensions": {
                "category": "graphql-input"
            }
        }
    ]
}
```

(`Maximum pageSize is X` — where X is the configured `maxPageSize` value, default 300)

---

## Actual result

Query executes without validation. `pageSize: 999` is accepted silently. No error is returned.

---

## Root cause

`SearchCriteriaValidator` (which enforces `maxPageSize: 300`) is registered
in `magento2-base/app/etc/di.xml` (primary config):

```xml
<!-- magento2-base/app/etc/di.xml -->
<type name="Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="validators" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="searchCriteriaValidator" xsi:type="object">
                Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\SearchCriteriaValidator
            </item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

`module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml` (module config) also defines `validators` for the
same type, but only with `backpressureValidator`:

```xml
<!-- module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml -->
<type name="Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator">
    <arguments>
        <argument name="validators" xsi:type="array">
            <item name="backpressureValidator" xsi:type="object">
                Magento\GraphQl\Model\Backpressure\BackpressureFieldValidator
            </item>
        </argument>
    </arguments>
</type>
```

Module-level DI configuration has higher priority than primary config.
When module config defines the same `xsi:type="array"` argument, it **replaces**
the primary config's array — it does **not** merge items. As a result,
`searchCriteriaValidator` is silently dropped.

**Verification at runtime:**

```php
$validator = $objectManager->get(
    \Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Query\Resolver\Argument\Validator\CompositeValidator::class
);
$ref = new ReflectionClass($validator);
$prop = $ref->getProperty('validators');
$prop->setAccessible(true);
var_dump(array_keys($prop->getValue($validator)));
// Output: ['backpressureValidator']
// Expected: ['searchCriteriaValidator', 'backpressureValidator']
```

Move `searchCriteriaValidator` registration **from** `magento2-base/app/etc/di.xml`
**to** `module-graph-ql/etc/di.xml`. Both validators should live at module level
so that future validators added by third-party modules can safely merge via
`xsi:type="array"`.

question_text:
## Preconditions

- Magento 2.4.8 (fresh install via `composer create-project`)

- Developer mode

## Steps to reproduce

1. Send any GraphQL mutation that uses variables with String-typed fields:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/graphql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Store: default' \
  -d '{
    "query": "mutation CreateCustomer($input: CustomerCreateInput!) { createCustomerV2(input: $input) { customer { id email } } }",

```

Or any query that returns scalar fields:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/graphql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ isEmailAvailable(email: \"test@example.com\") { is_email_available } }"}'
```

## Expected result

Mutation creates customer and returns data. Query returns `is_email_available: true/false`.

```json
    "message": "Internal server error",
    "extensions": {

    }
```

ISSUE #40616: GraphQL typeLoader fails to resolve built-in scalar types (String, Boolean, Int, Float, ID)
Author: florinel-chis
Date: 2026-03-22T09:29:40Z
Labels: Issue: ready for confirmation
State: closed

[c0]
## Preconditions

- Magento 2.4.8 (fresh install via `composer create-project`)
- `webonyx/graphql-php` ^15.0
- Developer mode

## Steps to reproduce

1. Send any GraphQL mutation that uses variables with String-typed fields:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/graphql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Store: default' \
  -d '{
    "query": "mutation CreateCustomer($input: CustomerCreateInput!) { createCustomerV2(input: $input) { customer { id email } } }",
    "variables": { "input": { "firstname": "Test", "lastname": "User", "email": "test@example.com", "password": "Test1234!" } }
  }'
```

Or any query that returns scalar fields:

```bash
curl -s -X POST http://localhost:8080/graphql \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"query":"{ isEmailAvailable(email: \"test@example.com\") { is_email_available } }"}'
```

## Expected result

Mutation creates customer and returns data. Query returns `is_email_available: true/false`.

## Actual result

```json
{
  "errors": [{
    "message": "Internal server error",
    "extensions": {
      "debugMessage": "Config element \"String\" is not declared in GraphQL schema"
    }
  }]
}
```

The same error occurs for `Boolean`, `Int`, `Float`, and `ID` scalars.

## Root cause

In `vendor/magento/framework/GraphQl/Schema/SchemaGenerator.php`, the `typeLoader` closure delegates to `TypeRegistry::get()` for ALL type names, including built-in GraphQL scalar types:

```php
'typeLoader' => function ($name) {
    return $this->typeRegistry->get($name);  // throws for "String", "Boolean", etc.
},
```

`TypeRegistry::get()` calls `Config::getConfigElement('String')` which throws `LogicException` because built-in scalar types are not declared in Magento's `schema.graphqls` files — they're provided by the `webonyx/graphql-php` library itself.

In `webonyx/graphql-php` v15, `Schema::getType()` (line 328-349) calls the `typeLoader` first, then falls back to `Type::builtInScalars()`. But the fallback never executes because the `typeLoader` throws instead of returning `null`.

The `ScalarTypes` class at `Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Schema\Type\ScalarTypes` already has `isScalarType()` and `getScalarTypeInstance()` methods that correctly resolve built-in scalars, but they are never called by the `typeLoader`.

## Suggested fix

In `SchemaGenerator::generate()`, check for built-in scalars before delegating to `TypeRegistry`:

```php
'typeLoader' => function ($name) {
    $builtInScalars = \GraphQL\Type\Definition\Type::builtInScalars();
    if (isset($builtInScalars[$name])) {
        return $builtInScalars[$name];
    }
    return $this->typeRegistry->get($name);
},
```

This is a one-line fix that lets the `typeLoader` return the correct webonyx scalar type objects directly, bypassing the Magento config system for types it was never designed to handle.

ISSUE #40591: GraphQL queries fail with "Config element 'String' is not declared in GraphQL schema" after webonyx/graphql-php 15.31.0
Author: damienwebdev
Date: 2026-03-16T23:56:04Z
Labels: Issue: ready for confirmation, Reported on 2.4.x
State: closed

[c0]
### Preconditions and environment

                                                                                                                                                          
Magento 2.4.7-p9 with webonyx/graphql-php >= 15.31.0                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                          


### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce:                                                                                                                                     
 
1. Update webonyx/graphql-php to 15.31.0 or 15.31.1 (allowed by the ^15.0 constraint in magento/framework)                                              
2. Send any GraphQL query that uses variable definitions with scalar types (e.g. $search: String)

For Example:


```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://magento2.test:8000/graphql" \                                                                                                   
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \                                                                                                                 
    -d '{"query":"query($s:String){products(filter:{name:{match:$s}}){total_count}}","variables":{"s":"test"}}'  
```

### Expected result

Product count matching the queried name search.

### Actual result

  Internal server error: Config element "String" is not declared in GraphQL schema


### Additional information

In webonyx/graphql-php v15.31.0, the order of type resolution in Schema::getType() changed. Previously (v15.30.2):

// 1. Check standard types (String, Int, Float, Boolean, ID) first
// 2. Call typeLoader

After v15.31.0:
// 1. Call typeLoader
// 2. Check built-in scalars

Magento's SchemaGenerator (in magento/framework) registers a typeLoader callback that calls TypeRegistry::get() → Config::getConfigElement(). This throws a `LogicException` for built-in scalars like String because they aren't declared in Magento's GraphQL schema config. The exception prevents the `webonyx` library from falling through to its built-in scalar check.

Fix (in `magento/framework`):

In `Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Schema\SchemaGenerator::generate`, the typeLoader should return null for built-in GraphQL scalars:

```php
'typeLoader' => function ($name) {
    if (\GraphQL\Type\Definition\Type::getStandardTypes()[$name] ?? null) {
        return null;
    }
    return $this->typeRegistry->get($name);
},
```

## Workaround
Pin `webonyx/graphql-php` to 15.30.2 in composer.json.

This is also arguably a concern for `webonyx/graphql-php` since they broke a behavioral contract — typeLoaders that worked before now need to handle built-in scalars they never had to handle. But the fix is straightforward regardless.

comments.author: damienwebdev
comments.body:
### Preconditions and environment

                                                                                                                                                          
Magento 2.4.7-p9 with webonyx/graphql-php >= 15.31.0                                                                               
                                                                                                                                                          


### Steps to reproduce

Steps to reproduce:                                                                                                                                     
 
1. Update webonyx/graphql-php to 15.31.0 or 15.31.1 (allowed by the ^15.0 constraint in magento/framework)                                              
2. Send any GraphQL query that uses variable definitions with scalar types (e.g. $search: String)

For Example:


```bash
curl -s -X POST "http://magento2.test:8000/graphql" \                                                                                                   
    -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \                                                                                                                 
    -d '{"query":"query($s:String){products(filter:{name:{match:$s}}){total_count}}","variables":{"s":"test"}}'  
```

### Expected result

Product count matching the queried name search.

### Actual result

  Internal server error: Config element "String" is not declared in GraphQL schema


### Additional information

In webonyx/graphql-php v15.31.0, the order of type resolution in Schema::getType() changed. Previously (v15.30.2):

// 1. Check standard types (String, Int, Float, Boolean, ID) first
// 2. Call typeLoader

After v15.31.0:
// 1. Call typeLoader
// 2. Check built-in scalars

Magento's SchemaGenerator (in magento/framework) registers a typeLoader callback that calls TypeRegistry::get() → Config::getConfigElement(). This throws a `LogicException` for built-in scalars like String because they aren't declared in Magento's GraphQL schema config. The exception prevents the `webonyx` library from falling through to its built-in scalar check.

Fix (in `magento/framework`):

In `Magento\Framework\GraphQl\Schema\SchemaGenerator::generate`, the typeLoader should return null for built-in GraphQL scalars:

```php
'typeLoader' => function ($name) {
    if (\GraphQL\Type\Definition\Type::getStandardTypes()[$name] ?? null) {
        return null;
    }
    return $this->typeRegistry->get($name);
},
```

## Workaround
Pin `webonyx/graphql-php` to 15.30.2 in composer.json.

This is also arguably a concern for `webonyx/graphql-php` since they broke a behavioral contract — typeLoaders that worked before now need to handle built-in scalars they never had to handle. But the fix is straightforward regardless.

### Release note

_No response_

- [x] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._

- [ ] Severity: **S4** _- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”._

---------
### Description (*)
This PR is to fix an issue where the sri-hashes.json file can become corrupt due to a race condition that breaks checkout. The issue can happen randomly without warning, and currently the only way to fix it is to regenerate the sri-hashes.json file through redeploying static content. The proposed fix locks the sri-hashes.json to keep multiple processes from writing to the file, and also includes a check to remove the file if its corrupt. The fix comes from code written here: https://gist.github.com/hryvinskyi/3df14e684d67bd8f7d278f4340ab133b

N/A

N/A

### Manual testing scenarios (*)
NOTE: This is difficult to test because it is a race condition that happens randomly. Some ways that this can happen are:
1. When a customer access a page that requires hash generation while using concurrent requests.
2. High volume traffic that requires hash generation to happen.

### Questions or comments
Since this is difficult to test, I'm unsure about how to include testing instructions for this. I had originally reached out to Adobe support about this issue and asked about a patch for this issue that someone else wrote, but was told I needed to make a PR to get the Magento development team to review it.

title: Slow products API REST with huge products
need_summary: Whether the slow REST query on huge product catalogs needs the added `catalog_product_entity_int` index (`attribute_id, store_id, entity_id`), as referenced by GitHub pull request #38316 and the related issue #38315.
security_topic: performance regression in product API query indexing
question_text:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version : 2.4.8
- PHP version : 8.3
- Mariadb version : 15.1
- Linux Debian : 11.11
- Import a huge amount of products : ~30k

### Steps to reproduce

1- In Magento Admin > System > Integration > Create a new token
2- In terminal execute the following curl command : 
```
$ curl -g   -H "Authorization: Bearer xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx"   -w "\nTotal: %{time_total}s\n"   -o /dev/null -s   "https://mywebsite/rest/store_name/V1/custom/products?searchCriteria[current_page]=1&searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][conditionType]=neq&searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][field]=type_id&searchCriteria[filter_groups][0][filters][0][value]=configurable&searchCriteria[filter_groups][1][filters][0][conditionType]=gt&searchCriteria[filter_groups][1][filters][0][field]=visibility&searchCriteria[filter_groups][1][filters][0][value]=2&searchCriteria[filter_groups][2][filters][0][field]=status&searchCriteria[filter_groups][2][filters][0][value]=1&searchCriteria[filter_groups][3][filters][0][conditionType]=eq&searchCriteria[filter_groups][3][filters][0][field]=website_id&searchCriteria[filter_groups][3][filters][0][value]=3&searchCriteria[filter_groups][4][filters][0][conditionType]=eq&searchCriteria[filter_groups][4][filters][0][field]=store_id&searchCriteria[filter_groups][4][filters][0][value]=3&searchCriteria[pageSize]=100"
```
answer_text:
This sounds closely related to #38315, to fix that one, we have https://github.com/magento/magento2/pull/38316 which adds a new index, but only for the `attribute_id` & `entity_id` combo. Does that improve the situation as well for you @mbautista?

That PR was merged and will be included in Magento 2.4.9 which will [get released in a few months](https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/release/planning/schedule).

title: [Issue] Fix directory path served as file in `\Magento\MediaStorage\App\Media`
need_summary: Whether the directory-path request bug in Magento MediaStorage is still reproducible in released versions and what changed in `nginx.conf`/commit `de05aecb618c9d8676373323078e7232d0700014` to stop falling back to `get.php`.
security_topic: directory path served as file in media handling
question_text:
On `2.4.8-p3`, the issue **is reproducible**.

In this version, `nginx.conf` contains the `location /media/` block, which attempts to process any request URI starting with `/media/`.

The issue is caused by the rule:

```nginx
try_files $uri $uri/ /get.php$is_args$args;
```

This rule is not restricted by file type and is always executed, so any `/media/` request falls back to `get.php`.

Starting from commit https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/de05aecb618c9d8676373323078e7232d0700014, this global directive was commented out.
Now the redirect to `get.php` only happens when the requested media file matches the explicitly allowed file types.

---

Summary
- ❌ Reproducible on 2.4.8-p3
- ✅ Not reproducible on 2.4-develop

---

⚠️ Note

After commit https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/a4b9bdc3bfd4d097c79eb9c21c5106dbbdc04721, it looks like files inside `/media/` with the following extensions may no longer be accessible:

`zip`, `gz`, `gzip`, `bz2`, `csv`, `xml`

In this commit, the following block was modified and the fallback was commented out:

```nginx
location ~* \.(zip|gz|gzip|bz2|csv|xml)$ {
    ...
    # try_files $uri $uri/ /get.php$is_args$args; <----
    ...
}
```

Since `try_files` is now commented out, requests for these file types will not fall back to `get.php`.
As a result, if the file does not physically exist or requires Magento handling, it may return 404.
answer_text: We have tried to reproduce the issue in Latest 2.4-develop instance and we are not able to reproduce the issue.

comments.body:
This issue is automatically created based on existing pull request: magento/magento2#40467: Fix DivisionByZeroError in creditmemo tax for zero base shipping amount

---------
## Description

The `collect()` method in `Magento\Sales\Model\Order\Creditmemo\Total\Tax` has a partial guard at line 137 that checks `$orderShippingAmount > 0` before dividing at line 139, but line 140 divides by `$baseOrderShippingAmount` without any zero-check.

When an order has free shipping (`base_shipping_amount = 0`), this causes a `DivisionByZeroError` at line 140:

```php
$basePart = $creditmemo->getBaseShippingAmount() / $baseOrderShippingAmount;
```

This is inconsistent with line 109 in the same method, which correctly guards `$baseOrderShippingAmount` before dividing:

```php
if ($baseOrderShippingAmount && $creditmemo->getBaseShippingAmount() !== null) {
    $taxFactor = $creditmemo->getBaseShippingAmount() / $baseOrderShippingAmount;
```

## Steps to reproduce

1. Place an order with free shipping (`shipping_amount = 0`, `base_shipping_amount = 0`)
2. Create an invoice for the order
3. Trigger credit memo creation via `CreditmemoFactory::createByOrder()`
4. `DivisionByZeroError` is thrown at `Tax.php:140`

In production, this is triggered by the Stripe webhook retry cron (`stripe_webhook_events_retry`) when it attempts to cancel/refund an order with free shipping that has an existing invoice.

## Expected result

Credit memo is created without error. When shipping amounts are zero, the shipping tax proportion block is skipped entirely (no shipping tax to apportion).

## Actual result

```
DivisionByZeroError: Division by zero in vendor/magento/module-sales/Model/Order/Creditmemo/Total/Tax.php:140
```

This error repeats on every cron cycle, blocking webhook retry processing.

## Fix

Add `$baseOrderShippingAmount > 0` to the existing guard clause at line 137, so both divisors (`$orderShippingAmount` at line 139 and `$baseOrderShippingAmount` at line 140) are protected.

## Related

The invoice path (line 109) already has the correct guard. This fix makes the non-invoice path consistent.

title: Incorrect product price in PDP/PLP for customer group due to FPC still showing guest user's price
need_summary: Whether the 2.4.8-p3 full-page cache change that switched IdentifierInterface to IdentifierForSave can cause guest prices to be served to logged-in customer groups, as described in PR 40475 and the cited DI configuration.
security_topic: full-page-cache cache-key mismatch after login affecting customer-group pricing
question_text: PDP/PLP prices should immediately switch to the logged-in customer group price after login, because FPC should  vary by X-Magento-Vary and Magento\Framework\App\PageCache\Identifier should be used for cache lookup.
answer_text:
Try adding this in a global di.xml: 

``` 
    <!-- Fix FPC load to use the original Identifier (reads vary cookie from request).
         Magento 2.4.8-p4 changed the global IdentifierInterface preference to IdentifierForSave
         which uses HttpContext — empty at load time, causing all pages to share the same cache key. -->
    <type name="Magento\Framework\App\PageCache\Kernel">
        <arguments>
            <argument name="identifier" xsi:type="object">Magento\Framework\App\PageCache\Identifier</argument>
        </arguments>
    </type>
```

From what I can see 2.4.8 has changed the cachekey identifier to Magento\Framework\App\PageCache\IdentifierForSave which never looks at the Magento-X-Vary cookie.

### Preconditions and environment

### Steps to reproduce

  1. Configure a customer group to have a customer-group price for a product, then browse the product page as guest.

The PDP/PLP prices should immediately switch to the logged-in customer group price after login, because FPC should  vary by X-Magento-Vary and Magento\Framework\App\PageCache\Identifier should be used for cache lookup.

comments.author: m2-assistant
comments.body:
This issue is automatically created based on existing pull request: magento/magento2#40435: Validate string collection filters to prevent SQL injection

---------
## Harden collection string filters against SQL injection

### Summary
This PR addresses a SQL injection risk in Magento’s collection filtering
system related to the `'string'` filter type.

The collection API allows raw SQL fragments to be passed when using
`addFilter(..., 'string')`. These fragments were previously applied
directly to the query without validation, relying entirely on developer
discipline to ensure proper escaping.

While Magento core uses this API safely, the design created a dangerous
footgun for custom and third-party code.

---

### Root Cause
The `'string'` filter type accepts arbitrary SQL fragments and passes
them directly to the database layer via `$select->where()` with no
validation or enforcement.

This makes it easy for unsafe code paths to introduce SQL injection if
user-controlled input is passed without proper escaping.

---

### Fix
This change introduces validation for `'string'` filters before they are
applied to the query:

- Unsafe SQL patterns are rejected with a clear exception
- Properly escaped SQL fragments (e.g. generated via `quoteInto()`)
  continue to work unchanged
- No behavior change for existing safe Magento core code

**Files updated:**
- `Magento/Framework/Data/Collection/AbstractDb.php`
- `Magento/Framework/Data/Collection/SqlInjectionValidator.php` (new)

---

### Security Impact
- Prevents SQL injection through unsafe use of collection string filters
- Hardens the framework against vulnerable third-party extensions
- Enforces secure-by-default behavior at the framework level
- Provides defense-in-depth without breaking existing safe usage

---

### Compatibility
- Fully backward compatible for correct implementations
- Magento core code unaffected
- Only unsafe usage patterns are blocked
- Clear error messaging guides developers to safer APIs

We've looked into the reported issues and wanted to share our analysis. 1. it does NOT provide tracking information We've confirmed this behavior. In TrackingService.php, the logic discards the response body when the HTTP status code is ≥ 400. As a result, error details (including 4xx/5xx responses) are not propagated, which leads to the blank tracking behavior. We regard this as a valid bug and are treating it as a code-level fix. 2. It doesn't preserve the Allowed Methods settings if the API choice is changed. We've confirmed this as well. When switching between USPS Web Tools and REST APIs, the Allowed Methods configuration is not preserved. This can be addressed in code by persisting these values (e.g., via backend models and configuration handling) when the API type changes. We consider this a valid defect and plan to fix it at the module level. 3. it does not report or protect against the "429" Quota limit result. We investigated this and found that the 429 quota is enforced by USPS at the API level, not by the Magento USPS module. The flow is: During checkout and on the cart page, when the customer changes country or enters/updates the postal code, Magento's core checkout triggers estimate-shipping-methods. That request results in rate-quote calls to all active carriers, including USPS. Each such change (after debouncing) generates a new USPS API request. The 429 response is returned when the USPS quota is exceeded. Because the limit is defined and enforced by USPS, it is not something we can change from the Magento side. We've also found external references that discuss these limits, e.g.: https://www.smarty.com/blog/usps-api-rate-limit We would welcome any suggestions from the community. --- [c22] @bluedarter2 2026-03-09T20:21:52Z: @cod62627 Please note the following: > 1. it does NOT provide tracking information > We've confirmed this behavior. Yes we *know* the limit is a USPS limit. As I mentioned, the implementation needs to protect against unneeded API calls! So, for instance don't perform a USPS API call until there is a complete zip code in the field. Also, since opening this PR there have been other issues with the implementation discovered, including the weight calculation. The token is valid 8 hours. Cache it in Magento's cache backend and you eliminate 99% of wasted requests. The tracking failure is because `_parseTrackingResponse()` still calls `simplexml_load_string()` on a JSON response. v3 returns JSON, not XML — so it silently returns false and tracking shows "not found." Wrote up the full breakdown with a drop-in token caching module: https://revaddress.com/blog/magento-usps-ac15210-fix Rate limit architecture (why 60/hr and how to handle it): https://revaddress.com/blog/usps-api-rate-limits-2026-what-changed --- [c24] @jtalk22 2026-03-10T12:32:47Z: I've been working through the v3 migration for a different stack and hit the same wall. A few things that might help people here while Adobe works on the official fix: **Why tracking is broken:** AC-15210 swapped the USPS base URL to `apis.usps.com/tracking/v3/` but `_parseTrackingResponse()` still calls `simplexml_load_string()` on the response. The v3 API returns JSON, not XML — so it silently fails and shows "tracking not found." The fix is replacing the XML parser with `json_decode()` and mapping the new response fields (`trackingEvents` array instead of `` nodes). **Why you're hitting 429s:** The v3 API enforces ~60 requests/hour by default (the old Web Tools API had no practical limit). AC-15210 requests a fresh OAuth token on *every single API call* instead of caching it. Each token is valid for 8 hours, so you're burning through your rate limit on auth calls alone. Here's the fix: ```php // Cache the OAuth token in Magento's cache backend $cached = $this->cache->load('usps_oauth_v3_token'); if ($cached) { return $cached; // No HTTP call needed } // Only fetch when cache is empty $response = $this->httpClient->post('https://apis.usps.com/oauth2/v3/token', [ 'grant_type' => 'client_credentials', 'client_id' => $clientId, 'client_secret' => $clientSecret, 'scope' => 'addresses tracking prices', ]); $data = json_decode($response); // Cache with 30-min buffer before expiry $this->cache->save($data->access_token, 'usps_oauth_v3_token', [], $data->expires_in - 1800); return $data->access_token; ``` **Rate field mapping:** The v3 pricing endpoint returns `mailClass: "PRIORITY_MAIL"` and `totalBasePrice` — different from the old `Priority Mail` and `` XML structure. If your allowed methods config references the old service names, rates come back empty. **Requesting higher limits:** You can email USPS at their Web Tools inquiry form (https://emailus.usps.com/s/web-tools-inquiry) to request a rate limit increase. They do grant them for production applications. I wrote up the full breakdown of what AC-15210 changes and what it misses here: https://revaddress.com/blog/magento-usps-ac15210-fix — includes the field mapping table and a drop-in token caching module. The rate limit architecture is covered separately: https://revaddress.com/blog/usps-api-rate-limits-2026-what-changed --- [c25] @warmoth-dev 2026-03-11T15:48:30Z: After encountering some issues with priority mail international not populating I found that module-usps/Model/ShippingMethodManager is missing the method for PRIORITY_MAIL_INTERNATIONAL_MACHINABLE_ISC_SINGLE-PIECE --- [c26] @jaywilliams 2026-03-11T20:26:56Z: @warmoth-dev Yes, I've been looking into this issue as well, I'm working updated patch which resolves this issue, by removing the NONSTANDARD/MACHINABLE wording. --- [c27] @cod62627 2026-03-12T14:39:04Z: @bluedarter2 > > Yes we _know_ the limit is a USPS limit. As I mentioned, the implementation needs to protect against unneeded API calls! So, for instance don't perform a USPS API call until there is a complete zip code in the field. > > Also, since opening this PR there have been other issues with the implementation discovered, including the weight calculation. Hopefully you have (or will) review all the discussions/comments in this PR and the related one ([#39991 (comment)](https://github.com/magento/magento2/issues/39991#issuecomment-3788153643)). We have updated the logic to restrict USPS API requests based on postal code length. Since postal code lengths may vary by country/region, a conditional check has been added so that the USPS request is triggered only when the postal code length is greater than 4 characters. This approach reduces unnecessary API calls during typing and helps prevent hitting the USPS request limit prematurely. Regarding the Weight issue: Currently, Magento still relies on the legacy weight_pounds / weight_ounces model even when sending REST requests. Because of this, when weight_pounds evaluates to 0, the code applies the fallback: **(0) ?: 1** as a result, any weight under 1 lb is automatically treated as 1 lb. We have reviewed the USPS and updated the Carrier.php and ShipmentService.php and verified calculated quote rate through Postman and in Magento Now, with same originZIPCode, destinationZIPCode and product weight (**0.1 lbs**) in both postman and magento we are getting same rate $5.89 --- [c28] @jaywilliams 2026-03-12T15:59:39Z: @warmoth-dev @cod62627 Here's the updated `processShippingRateForItem()` method in the *Model/ShipmentService.php*, which incorporates a fix for Priority Mail International quotes. _(Note the added preg_match() call)_ ``` php /** * Processing rate for ship element * * @param array $rateElement * @param array $costArr */ private function processShippingRateForItem( array $rateElement, array &$costArr ): void { if (empty($rateElement['productName']) && empty($rateElement['description'])) { return; } $productName = $rateElement['description']; // Standardize international service names if (preg_match('/Priority Mail( Express)? International (Nonstandard|Machinable) ISC Single-piece/', $productName, $matches)) { $productName = "Priority Mail" . ($matches[1] ?? '') . " International ISC Single-piece"; } $methodCode = strtoupper(substr($this->replaceSpaceWithUnderscore($productName), 0, 120)); $methodTitle = $this->shippingMethodManager->getMethodTitle($methodCode); $allowedMethods = $this->getRestAllowedMethods(); if (in_array($methodCode, array_keys($allowedMethods))) { // Use totalPrice if available, otherwise use price $cost = isset($rateElement['totalPrice']) ? (float)$rateElement['totalPrice'] : (float)$rateElement['price']; $costArr[$methodCode] = [ 'price' => $cost, 'code' => $methodCode, 'productName' => $methodTitle ]; } } ``` I also updated the `getJsonQuotes()` method with a minimum Postal Code/ZIP limit, to reduce the number of unnecessary API requests. *(Note the different minimums for US/International addresses)* ```php if ($this->carrierModel->_isUSCountry($request->getDestCountryId())) { $requestParam['destinationZIPCode'] = is_string($request->getDestPostal()) ? substr($request->getDestPostal(), 0, 5) : ''; // Skip API request if ZIP code is incomplete if (strlen(trim($requestParam['destinationZIPCode'])) < 5) { return $this->_parseJsonResponse([]); } } else { $requestParam['destinationCountryCode'] = $request->getDestCountryId(); $requestParam['foreignPostalCode'] = $request->getDestPostal() ?? ''; // Skip API request if postal code is incomplete if (strlen(trim($requestParam['foreignPostalCode'])) < 3) { return $this->_parseJsonResponse([]); } } ``` All of these fixes have been included in my backported AC-15210 patch for Magento v2.4.5-p14. https://gist.github.com/jaywilliams/97ca39652b917e95f22e1d29c85bb466 Hope that helps others out there with this rough Magento USPS rollout. --- [c29] @cod62627 2026-03-13T04:44:36Z: > The tracking information presented by Magento is incorrect. The issue is that the tracking information returned by USPS for each event includes: eventTimestamp, GMTTimestamp, and GMTOffset > > The eventTimestamp appears to reflect the correct local event date and time. In my case Hillsboro Oregon, which is GMT-8:00 The GMTTimestamp correctly reflects the event timestamp in GMT, and the GMTOffset is also correct. > > However the Tracking information displayed by Magento appears to have the wrong DateTimeZone, so the tracking is wrong! > > It seems to be using GMT as the DateTimeZone rather than the Locale set in Stores->Config->Generatl->Locale Options. > > ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7767099f-1e03-4381-9323-4931d63e9425) > > Thank you for reporting this and for sharing the details from shipping.log. We’ve reviewed the issue and confirmed that it is valid. The behavior you’re seeing comes from how we interpret the USPS REST API’s eventTimestamp field. USPS sends that value in the event’s local timezone (e.g., PST for Hillsboro, OR), using the GMTOffset field to indicate the offset. Our current logic does not use GMTOffset when parsing eventTimestamp, so the datetime is treated as if it were in the server’s default timezone (often UTC). That can cause the dates and times shown in the tracking popup to differ from what USPS reports (e.g., “4:05 pm on January 8, 2026 in HILLSBORO, OR”). We have implemented a fix that uses the GMTOffset field from the USPS response when parsing eventTimestamp, so the tracking popup displays the correct local date and time. Thank you again for bringing this to our attention and helping improve the USPS integration. --- [c30] @Anantkprajapati 2026-03-17T11:12:31Z: Missing USPS Shipping Method (Media Mail) **Preconditions & Environment** 1. Platform: Magento Open Source (version 2.4.7-p8 with AC-15210 patch applied) 2. USPS REST API credentials are properly configured in the Magento Admin 3. Required USPS shipping methods are enabled: - Media Mail - USPS Ground Advantage - Priority Mail **Steps to Reproduce** 1. Add a product to the shopping cart 2. Navigate to the Shopping Cart page 3. Enter a valid United States: - Country - State - ZIP Code 4. Proceed to view available shipping methods **Expected Result** All configured USPS shipping methods should be displayed: - Media Mail - USPS Ground Advantage - Priority Mail **Actual Result** Only the following shipping methods are displayed: - USPS Ground Advantage - Priority Mail If is there any solution or patch file then please know me. Thanks, --- [c31] @cod62627 2026-03-19T08:36:05Z: @Anantkprajapati Thank you for reporting the missing Media Mail shipping method on the cart and checkout pages. We’ve investigated and implemented a fix. Root cause: The USPS REST API v3 returns several Media Mail variants (e.g. “Media Mail Nonstandard Basic”, “Media Mail Machinable 5-digit”, “Media Mail Nonstandard 5-digit”), while Magento’s configuration uses a single canonical code (MEDIA_MAIL_MACHINABLE_5-DIGIT). The mapping logic in ShipmentService.php did not correctly normalize these variants to the configured method code, so Media Mail rates were not shown even when the method was enabled in Admin. We appreciate your patience and your detailed report, which helped us identify and fix the issue. --- [c32] @engcom-Bravo 2026-03-27T08:22:12Z: "The Adobe Commerce Engineering team has reviewed this issue and confirmed that it has been resolved through an internally created fix that has now been delivered. Please refer to the GitHub public link below for more details. If you have any further questions, feel free to leave a comment. Thank you!" Note – Backporting of this change for versions 2.4.8, 2.4.7, and 2.4.6 is currently in progress, and we are targeting its availability in the upcoming respective security patch releases. Github public link: https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amagento%2Fmagento2+AC-15210+doesn%27t+seem+complete.+USPS+REST+api+required+in+less+than+a+month.&type=commits --- [c33] @devvolunteeruk 2026-04-21T08:27:13Z: The following patch will fix the 1lb issue, where products weighting less than 1lb do not have the USPS shipping options at checkout. ``` diff --git a/vendor/magento/module-usps/Model/ShipmentService.php b/vendor/magento/module-usps/Model/ShipmentService.php index 02ccf7da..cee26b47 100644 --- a/vendor/magento/module-usps/Model/ShipmentService.php +++ b/vendor/magento/module-usps/Model/ShipmentService.php @@ -204,8 +204,14 @@ class ShipmentService ]; foreach ($request->getPackages() as $packageData) { + + $weight = isset($packageData['weight_pounds']) && $packageData['weight_pounds'] > 0 + ? (float) $packageData['weight_pounds'] + : (float) ($packageData['weight_ounces'] ?? 16) / 16; + $requestParam['packageDescription'] = [ - "weight" => $packageData['weight_pounds'] ?? 1, + // "weight" => $packageData['weight_pounds'] ?? 1, + "weight" => $weight, "mailClass" => 'ALL' ]; $requestParam['packageDescription']['length'] = $request->getLength() ? (int) $request->getLength() : 1; ``` Note that you first need to patch the USPS module using the quality patches tool, then apply the patch above. To enforce the correct sequence of patches, you can use the following in composer.json: ``` "scripts": { "post-install-cmd": [ "./vendor/bin/magento-patches apply AC-15210", "@apply-custom-patches" ], "post-update-cmd": [ "./vendor/bin/magento-patches apply AC-15210", "@apply-custom-patches" ], "apply-custom-patches": [ "patch -p1 < patches/composer/module-usps-sub-1-pound-weight.patch" ] } ``` Additional note - if you have a list of existing patches in your composer.json under 'extra', then they will execute first, followed by the quality patches AC-15210, and finally the module-usps patch above ---

comments.body: ### Preconditions and environment - 2.4.7-p8 with AC-15210 applied - REST API credentials entered into backend, and allowed methods configured This patch isn't ready for production use: 1) it does NOT provide tracking information 2) It doesn't preserve the Allowed Methods settings if the API choice is changed. 3) it should protect against sending unneeded requests to the USPS API, because: 4) it does not report or protect against the "429" Quota limit result. Hitting the limit means no rates are returned from the interface. If you are presenting rates to a customer, this is a disaster. Here is an example from the debug.log of a tracking request. It doesn't look like it's even POSTing a proper tracking request. This doesn't appear to have ANY of the information required by the REST api for a tracking request: ``` [2025-12-25T21:03:42.453158+00:00] main.DEBUG: array ( '9400136106195372355532' => array ( 'request' => '{}', 'result' => '', ), ) [] [] ``` Here is an example quota limit exceeded result, after too many requests have been sent to the USPS API portal. ``` 'request' => array ( 'originZIPCode' => '97123', 'pricingOptions' => array ( 0 => array ( 'priceType' => 'RETAIL', ), ), 'packageDescription' => array ( 'weight' => 1, 'mailClass' => 'ALL', 'length' => 1, 'height' => 1, 'width' => 1, 'girth' => 1, ), 'destinationZIPCode' => '97007', ), 'result' => ' { "apiVersion": "/shipments/v3", "error": { "code": "429", "message": "Exceeded quota limit. Please contact https://emailus.usps.com/s/web-tools-inquiry and a representative will assist.", "errors": [{"title":"Too Many Requests.","detail":"Quota limit exceeded. The number of requests has exceeded the quota established for the time period.","status":"429","source":{"parameter":"API product or default","APIProduct":"Public Access I"}}] } } ', ) [] [] ``` ### Steps to reproduce Running 2.4.6 or newer, install quality patch AC-15210 Go to Configuration->Sales->Delivery Methods->USPS Switch USPS type to USPS REST APIs, enter credentials, choose Allowed Methods, etc. Try tracking a previously-shipped parcel through the backend. ### Expected result 1. You should get proper tracking information. 2. You should be able to switch between USPS WEBtools api and REST api, and have your settings retained. 3. It needs to protect against sending unneeded requests, so that the vendor's quota isn't exceeded, 4. Because if the quota is exceeded, the interface refuses to produce shipping rate quotes - and the CUSTOMER will not see shipping rates to choose from on the front end. ### Actual result 1. No tracking, no tracking request POSTed or request is incomplete 2. Backend Allowed Methods not preserved when switching APIs 3. Sends lots of requests, risks vendor reaching USPS quote quota limit ### Additional information _No response_ ### Release note _No response_ ### Triage and priority - [x] Severity: **S0** _- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S3** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S4** _- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”._

Here's an update:
First off, after applying patch AC-15210 I made the changes as mentioned in this issue comment and the one following it:
https://github.com/magento/magento2/issues/39991#issuecomment-3365026364 

**For Tracking:** you MUST request access to the **USPS "Shipping Suite" API Product**!  By default they (USPS) will give you access to the "Public Access" API product which does NOT give you tracking access.

I just had USPS change my access level to "Shipping Suite", and now the tracking works.

comments.author: cod62627
comments.body:
@bluedarter2 

Thank you for raising this. We've looked into the reported issues and wanted to share our analysis.

1. it does NOT provide tracking information
We've confirmed this behavior. In TrackingService.php, the logic discards the response body when the HTTP status code is ≥ 400. As a result, error details (including 4xx/5xx responses) are not propagated, which leads to the blank tracking behavior. We regard this as a valid bug and are treating it as a code-level fix.
2. It doesn't preserve the Allowed Methods settings if the API choice is changed. 
We've confirmed this as well. When switching between USPS Web Tools and REST APIs, the Allowed Methods configuration is not preserved. This can be addressed in code by persisting these values (e.g., via backend models and configuration handling) when the API type changes. We consider this a valid defect and plan to fix it at the module level.
3. it does not report or protect against the "429" Quota limit result.
We investigated this and found that the 429 quota is enforced by USPS at the API level, not by the Magento USPS module. The flow is:
During checkout and on the cart page, when the customer changes country or enters/updates the postal code, Magento's core checkout triggers estimate-shipping-methods.
That request results in rate-quote calls to all active carriers, including USPS.
Each such change (after debouncing) generates a new USPS API request.
The 429 response is returned when the USPS quota is exceeded.

Because the limit is defined and enforced by USPS, it is not something we can change from the Magento side. We've also found external references that discuss these limits, e.g.:

https://www.smarty.com/blog/usps-api-rate-limit

We would welcome any suggestions from the community.

comments.author: jtalk22
comments.body:
The 429s are a token caching issue — AC-15210 fetches a fresh OAuth token on every API call instead of caching it. The token is valid 8 hours. Cache it in Magento's cache backend and you eliminate 99% of wasted requests.

The tracking failure is because `_parseTrackingResponse()` still calls `simplexml_load_string()` on a JSON response. v3 returns JSON, not XML — so it silently returns false and tracking shows "not found."

Wrote up the full breakdown with a drop-in token caching module: https://revaddress.com/blog/magento-usps-ac15210-fix

Rate limit architecture (why 60/hr and how to handle it): https://revaddress.com/blog/usps-api-rate-limits-2026-what-changed

comments.body: @bluedarter2 > > Yes we _know_ the limit is a USPS limit. As I mentioned, the implementation needs to protect against unneeded API calls! So, for instance don't perform a USPS API call until there is a complete zip code in the field. > > Also, since opening this PR there have been other issues with the implementation discovered, including the weight calculation. Hopefully you have (or will) review all the discussions/comments in this PR and the related one ([#39991 (comment)](https://github.com/magento/magento2/issues/39991#issuecomment-3788153643)). We have updated the logic to restrict USPS API requests based on postal code length. Since postal code lengths may vary by country/region, a conditional check has been added so that the USPS request is triggered only when the postal code length is greater than 4 characters. This approach reduces unnecessary API calls during typing and helps prevent hitting the USPS request limit prematurely. Regarding the Weight issue: Currently, Magento still relies on the legacy weight_pounds / weight_ounces model even when sending REST requests. Because of this, when weight_pounds evaluates to 0, the code applies the fallback: **(0) ?: 1** as a result, any weight under 1 lb is automatically treated as 1 lb. We have reviewed the USPS and updated the Carrier.php and ShipmentService.php and verified calculated quote rate through Postman and in Magento Now, with same originZIPCode, destinationZIPCode and product weight (**0.1 lbs**) in both postman and magento we are getting same rate $5.89

cod62627
comments.body: > The tracking information presented by Magento is incorrect. The issue is that the tracking information returned by USPS for each event includes: eventTimestamp, GMTTimestamp, and GMTOffset > > The eventTimestamp appears to reflect the correct local event date and time. In my case Hillsboro Oregon, which is GMT-8:00 The GMTTimestamp correctly reflects the event timestamp in GMT, and the GMTOffset is also correct. > > However the Tracking information displayed by Magento appears to have the wrong DateTimeZone, so the tracking is wrong! > > It seems to be using GMT as the DateTimeZone rather than the Locale set in Stores->Config->Generatl->Locale Options. > > ![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/7767099f-1e03-4381-9323-4931d63e9425) > > Thank you for reporting this and for sharing the details from shipping.log. We’ve reviewed the issue and confirmed that it is valid. The behavior you’re seeing comes from how we interpret the USPS REST API’s eventTimestamp field. USPS sends that value in the event’s local timezone (e.g., PST for Hillsboro, OR), using the GMTOffset field to indicate the offset. Our current logic does not use GMTOffset when parsing eventTimestamp, so the datetime is treated as if it were in the server’s default timezone (often UTC). That can cause the dates and times shown in the tracking popup to differ from what USPS reports (e.g., “4:05 pm on January 8, 2026 in HILLSBORO, OR”). We have implemented a fix that uses the GMTOffset field from the USPS response when parsing eventTimestamp, so the tracking popup displays the correct local date and time. Thank you again for bringing this to our attention and helping improve the USPS integration.

comments.author: cod62627
comments.body:
@Anantkprajapati 

Thank you for reporting the missing Media Mail shipping method on the cart and checkout pages. We’ve investigated and implemented a fix.

Root cause:

The USPS REST API v3 returns several Media Mail variants (e.g. “Media Mail Nonstandard Basic”, “Media Mail Machinable 5-digit”, “Media Mail Nonstandard 5-digit”), while Magento’s configuration uses a single canonical code (MEDIA_MAIL_MACHINABLE_5-DIGIT). The mapping logic in ShipmentService.php did not correctly normalize these variants to the configured method code, so Media Mail rates were not shown even when the method was enabled in Admin.

We appreciate your patience and your detailed report, which helped us identify and fix the issue.

need_summary: Whether the PayPal_Braintree sales order grid filtering bug is already covered by the published Adobe patch KB KA-27163 for Magento 2.4.8-p3.
security_topic: Sales order grid filtering broken by PayPal Braintree SQL rewrite
question_text: ### Preconditions and environment Magento Version: Magento Open Source 2.4.8-p3 PHP Version: PHP 8.4.15 ### Steps to reproduce 1. In Magento Admin, go to Sales → Orders 2. Select the 'Purchase Date' filter, and apply the filter. ### Expected result Display orders by purchase date after filter. ### Actual result An error message is displayed, indicating that the filter is invalid or not supported. ### Additional information The PayPal_Braintree module introduces a plugin on vendor/paypal/module-braintree-core/Plugin/SalesOrderGridPlugin.php which rewrites SQL WHERE conditions incorrectly. When the order grid is filtered by Created At, the plugin attempts to rewrite: ``` `created_at` → `main_table`.`created_at` ``` However, if the condition already contains a table alias, the plugin rewrites it again, causing the final SQL to become: ``` (((`main_table`.`main_table`.`created_at` >= '2025-11-30 12:00:00'))) ``` This produces invalid SQL and breaks the order grid. **Affected File**: vendor/paypal/module-braintree-core/Plugin/SalesOrderGridPlugin.php **Problematic Code** ```$wherePart[$key] = str_replace("`created_at`", "`main_table`.`created_at`", $condition);``` This code runs even when the condition already contains ``` `main_table`.`created_at` ``` leading to: ``` `main_table`.`main_table`.`created_at` ```
answer_text:
Hi @oxochenxa,

There is a patch already release regarding this issue https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-cloud-kcs/kbarticles/ka-27163 please try to apply this patch and let us know if you are still facing any issue.Hence we are closing this issue.

Thanks.

When the order grid is filtered by Created At, the plugin attempts to rewrite: ``` `created_at` → `main_table`.`created_at` ``` However, if the condition already contains a table alias, the plugin rewrites it again, causing the final SQL to become: ``` (((`main_table`.`main_table`.`created_at` >= '2025-11-30 12:00:00'))) ``` This produces invalid SQL and breaks the order grid. **Affected File**: vendor/paypal/module-braintree-core/Plugin/SalesOrderGridPlugin.php **Problematic Code** ```$wherePart[$key] = str_replace("`created_at`", "`main_table`.`created_at`", $condition);``` This code runs even when the condition already contains ``` `main_table`.`created_at` ``` leading to: ``` `main_table`.`main_table`.`created_at` ``` ### Release note _No response_ ### Triage and priority - [ ] Severity: **S0** _- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._ - [x] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S3** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S4** _- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”._

title: PaymentServicesPaypal module implicitly depends on InventoryInStorePickupFrontend module and breaks the checkout
need_summary: Whether the checkout break from the missing `isStorePickup` function in `magento/module-payment-services-paypal` v2.13.0 was fixed by the template change in v2.14.0 (`typeof isStorePickup !== 'function' || !isStorePickup()`).
security_topic: implicit dependency causing checkout template error
question_text: Magento_PaymentServicesPaypal module has implicit dependency on logic of Magento_InventoryInStorePickupFrontend module but it has no explicit dependency defined in module.xml
answer_text:
@engcom-Bravo I do see an issue on `magento/module-payment-services-paypal` v2.13.0 but there is no issue on v2.14.0. It was fixed somewhere in between

file: `vendor/magento/module-payment-services-paypal/view/frontend/web/template/shipping-information.html`
**v2.13.0**
```
<!-- ko if: (!isStorePickup()) -->
```
**v2.14.0**
```
<!-- ko if: (typeof isStorePickup !== 'function' || !isStorePickup()) -->
```

ISSUE #40346: PaymentServicesPaypal module implicitly depends on InventoryInStorePickupFrontend module and breaks the checkout Author: martin-cod Date: 2025-12-05T15:12:19Z Labels: Issue: needs update, Reported on 2.4.7-P8 State: closed [c0] ### Preconditions and environment - Magento version 2.4.7-p8 - Payment Services module version 2.13.0 - `Magento_InventoryInStorePickupFrontend` module is disabled as well as other `Magento_Inventory*` modules ### Steps to reproduce 1. Add product to cart 2. Go to checkout 3. Fill in shipping information and go to Payment step 4. Review Shipping Information in Order Summary block ### Expected result Shipping Information visible and displays the actual Shipping data as it was on Payment Services module version 2.11.0 ### Actual result Shipping Information is empty, JS error in console ### Additional information There is a mixin `vendor/magento/module-inventory-in-store-pickup-frontend/view/frontend/web/js/view/shipping-information-ext.js` where `isStorePickup` function is declared. Since `Magento_InventoryInStorePickupFrontend` module is disabled mixin is not loaded. `Magento_PaymentServicesPaypal` module adds another mixin `vendor/magento/module-payment-services-paypal/view/frontend/web/js/view/shipping-information-mixin.js` and original `shipping-information.html` template is overwritten. title: UPS Shipping Rate Issue: Shipping Method Selected but Rate Becomes $0, and Checkout Shows No Methods in the magento 2.4.1
need_summary: Whether Magento 2.4.1 must switch from the legacy UPS SOAP integration to the REST/OAuth2-based UPS type because the old integration is deprecated for security reasons, with the answer anchored by the Adobe Commerce UPS shipping documentation and the linked Experience League KB article.
security_topic: UPS shipping integration deprecation and OAuth 2.0 migration
question_text:
Hello,
Currently, I can't update the Magento version.
As a patch is available for the 2.4.4 - 2.4.6.
How can I manage it in the current Magento version 2.4.1?

Thank you.
answer_text:
Hello @vsakariya ,

Thank you for the response and You should update the Magento version. For the 2.4.7 release, UPS Type is removed because UPS and UPS XML types are scheduled for deprecation and UPS REST is the default. The United Parcel Service (UPS) APIs used by the native Adobe Commerce integration are temporarily deprecated because it does not currently support the OAuth 2.0 security model.

Hence we are proceeding with closing the issue and do let me know if you have any other questions

Thank you!

title: Properly handle multibyte characters in postcode templates for tax calculation
need_summary: Whether the postcode multibyte collation/UTF-8 failure is the same issue already addressed by issue #40138 and pending fix PR #40142.
security_topic: multibyte character handling causing checkout/tax calculation failure
question_text:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento 2.4.8-p3


### Steps to reproduce

1. Add product to cart
2. Go to checkout as guest
3. Enter "31000 Šibenik" as postcode

### Expected result

There are available shipping methods and you can proceed to the next step.

### Actual result

1. Observe that "estimate-shipping-methods" ajax call returns errors 500 with message "Unable to serialize value. Error: Malformed UTF-8 characters, possibly incorrectly encoded"
2. Check logs and observe that there is a MySQL DB error

title: Radio buttons on shipping method checkout page not clickable
need_summary: Whether the checkout shipping-method radio-button issue in Magento 2.4.8-p3 was caused by the payment-services-paypal module and is fixed by the referenced patch, per the 2.4.8-p3 release notes and the linked patch comment.
security_topic: checkout shipping method radio button clickability regression
question_text:
Radio buttons on shipping method checkout page not clickable
Clicking on the label next to the button works correct, but not directly on radio buttons.
Using Magento ver. 2.4.8-p3 with Porto theme
answer_text:
The problem is caused by updates to the magento/module-payment-services-paypal 2.13.0 module.

The mixin that was added to Magento_PaymentServicesPaypal/js/view/shipping-mixin overwrites the selectShippingMethod function. The original function returns true, while the mixin returns nothing.

To fix the error, apply the following patch:
[fix-selecting-shipping-method.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23613884/fix-selecting-shipping-method.patch)

comments.author: J-Wick4
comments.body:
Just encountered this issue tonight when testing a site before going live. It took me about an hour with Windsurf to solve the problem.

Here's the summary on how it was solved.


## Summary

**Problem:** Radio buttons on the checkout shipping methods page weren't visually responding to clicks, despite the selection working functionally.

**Root Cause:** The Knockout `checked` binding on the radio inputs was trying to write to `element.isSelected`, which is a read-only computed observable. This caused clicks directly on the radio button to fail silently.

**Solution Applied:**
1. Wrapped radio buttons in `<label>` elements with the `click="element.selectShippingMethod"` handler
2. Added `pointer-events: none` to the radio inputs so clicks pass through to the label
3. The label's click handler properly updates the shipping selection via Magento's API
4. The radio button's visual state updates automatically via the Knockout binding

**Additional UX Improvements:**
- Enlarged radio buttons (20x20px)
- Added `cursor: pointer` to all clickable cells
- Tightened spacing between radio button and price columns

**File Modified:**
- [/app/design/frontend/Smartwave/porto_child/Magento_Checkout/web/template/shipping-address/shipping-method-item.html](cci:7://file:///var/www/vhosts/domain.com/subdomains/store/app/design/frontend/Smartwave/porto_child/Magento_Checkout/web/template/shipping-address/shipping-method-item.html:0:0-0:0)

>

I just had Windsurf create the patch with the changes I made to my store that work perfectly. 

**Subject: [PATCH] Fix shipping method radio buttons not responding to clicks**

This patch fixes a bug where radio buttons on the checkout shipping method
selection do not visually indicate they are selected when clicked directly.
The underlying shipping method IS selected, but the radio button doesn't
show it.

ROOT CAUSE:
The Knockout `checked` binding on the radio inputs attempts to write to
`element.isSelected`, which is a read-only computed observable. This causes
clicks directly on the radio button to fail silently, while clicking
elsewhere on the row (which triggers selectShippingMethod) works correctly.

Additionally, the original template sets the `checked` attribute via:
  attr="'checked': element.rates().length == 1 || element.isSelected"
Since `element.isSelected` returns a string (the selected method code),
this evaluates to truthy for ALL radio buttons, causing visual confusion.

SOLUTION:
1. Wrap radio button in a <label> with click handler for selectShippingMethod
2. Add pointer-events: none to radio input so clicks pass through to label
3. Remove the problematic 'checked' attribute from the attr binding
4. Add explicit click handlers to all table cells for better UX
5. Enlarge radio buttons (20x20px) for easier mobile interaction

INSTALLATION:
Copy the patched file to your theme:
  app/design/frontend/<Vendor>/<Theme>/Magento_Checkout/web/template/shipping-address/shipping-method-item.html

Then run:
  bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f
  bin/magento cache:clean

Tested on: Magento 2.4.8-p3 with Porto theme

[fix-shipping-method-radio-buttons.patch](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/23956133/fix-shipping-method-radio-buttons.patch)

Navigate to any admin grid (Sales > Orders, Catalog > Products, etc.) 2. Modify column positions 3. Save the view ## What This Patch Does This patch backports the official fix from Magento's 2.4-develop branch by: 1. Adding a new `isPositionChanged()` method 2. **Status Update:** ✅ Already Fixed

I've investigated this issue and can confirm it's **already been resolved** in the `2.4-develop` branch.

**Fix Details:**
- The code was refactored to use a new `isPositionChanged()` method

- See: `app/code/Magento/Ui/Controller/Adminhtml/Bookmark/Save.php` lines 265-275

**However**, this fix is NOT in the 2.4.6-p12 release (current production version), which is why users are still experiencing this error.

comments.body:
# GitHub Issue Comment

## Status Update: ✅ Already Fixed in 2.4-develop

I've investigated this issue thoroughly and can confirm it's **already been resolved** in the `2.4-develop` branch.

### Fix Details

The Magento core team has refactored the code to use a new `isPositionChanged()` method that properly validates array keys before accessing them:

**File:** `app/code/Magento/Ui/Controller/Adminhtml/Bookmark/Save.php`

**New Method (lines 265-275):**
```php
private function isPositionChanged(array $existingConfig, array $currentConfig): bool
{
    foreach (['filters', 'positions'] as $key) {
        if (!array_key_exists($key, $existingConfig) || !array_key_exists($key, $currentConfig)) {
            return false;
        }
    }

    return $existingConfig['filters'] === $currentConfig['filters']
        && $existingConfig['positions'] !== $currentConfig['positions'];
}
```

This method uses `array_key_exists()` to safely check for the presence of `filters` and `positions` keys before attempting to access them, completely resolving the "Undefined array key" error.

### Current Status

- ✅ **Fixed in:** 2.4-develop branch
- ❌ **Not fixed in:** 2.4.6-p12 (current stable release)
- 📅 **Will be available in:** Magento 2.4.7 or later

### Workaround for 2.4.6-p12 Users

Since many users are still running 2.4.6-p12 in production and experiencing this error, I've created a **community patch** that backports this fix. See the patch file below.

### For Users on 2.4.6-p12

If you're experiencing this error on 2.4.6-p12, you can apply the community patch I've created (attached in next comment) until you're able to upgrade to 2.4.7+.

### Recommendation

- **For development:** Upgrade to 2.4-develop or wait for 2.4.7 release
- **For production:** Apply the community patch below
- **Long-term:** Plan upgrade to 2.4.7 when released

---

Should this issue be:
1. Closed as "Already Fixed" with a note about the upcoming release?
2. Kept open with a "Backport to 2.4.6-p* needed" label?

I'm happy to help with either direction!

# Community Patch for Magento 2.4.6-p12

For users experiencing the "Undefined array key 'filters'" error on Magento 2.4.6-p12, here's a backport of the fix from 2.4-develop.

## Installation Instructions

### Step 1: Download the Patch

Save the attached `magento-2.4.6-bookmark-undefined-filters-fix.patch` file to your `patches/` directory in your Magento root.

### Step 2: Update composer.json

Add the patch to your `composer.json` in the `extra.patches` section:

```json
{
    "extra": {
        "patches": {
            "magento/module-ui": {
                "Fix undefined array key 'filters' in Bookmark Save (backport from 2.4-develop)": "patches/magento-2.4.6-bookmark-undefined-filters-fix.patch"
            }
        }
    }
}
```

**Note:** If you already have patches for `magento/module-ui`, just add this as another entry.

### Step 3: Apply the Patch

```bash
# Run composer install to apply the patch
composer install

# Clear cache
php bin/magento cache:flush
```

### Step 4: Verify

The error should no longer appear in `var/log/exception.log` when you:
1. Navigate to any admin grid (Sales > Orders, Catalog > Products, etc.)
2. Modify column positions
3. Save the view

## What This Patch Does

This patch backports the official fix from Magento's 2.4-develop branch by:
1. Adding a new `isPositionChanged()` method
2. Using `array_key_exists()` to safely check for array keys before accessing them
3. Preventing PHP 8+ "Undefined array key" warnings

## Tested On

- ✅ Magento 2.4.6-p12
- ✅ PHP 8.1
- ✅ PHP 8.2

## Note

This is a temporary workaround. **Remove this patch** when you upgrade to Magento 2.4.7+ as the fix will be included natively.

question_text:
Upgrade Magento from 2.4.7-p7 to 2.4.7-p8 (apply patch, static content deploy for all locales/themes).

Ensure Redis cache and session backends are used; flush caches and sessions.

Clear pub/static/*, var/view_preprocessed/*. Deploy static content for all active locales/themes.

Access storefront checkout page (e.g., /de/checkout/ or /en/checkout/).

Observe checkout page fails to render (500 error) and an exception is logged with message:

Unable to unserialize value. Error: Syntax error
#1 Magento\Csp\Model\SubresourceIntegrityRepository->getData() called at …

Then flush all caches (or Redis cache DB) and re-open checkout — page works again.

Wait some time/daily usage or perform certain cache/asset operations → page fails again with the same error.
answer_text: An official patch was released: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/experience-cloud-kcs/kbarticles/ka-27997 (it looks like they've reverted some changes from the recent security patch to prevent this issue from happening because they probably didn't have enough time to find a proper working solution yet)

### Preconditions and environment

Magento version: 2.4.7-p8 (specifically patched state after applying p8 update)

PHP version: 8.3

Database: MySql 8.0.40

Cache/Session backend: Redis (separate system and session DBs)

Number of store views/locales: (e.g., 2 — de_DE and en_GB)

Deployment type: (Docker container, multi-web-node, full static content deploy)

Recent actions: Upgrade from 2.4.7-p7 to 2.4.7-p8, full static content deploy, then cache flush and Redis flush.


### Steps to reproduce

Upgrade Magento from 2.4.7-p7 to 2.4.7-p8 (apply patch, static content deploy for all locales/themes).

Ensure Redis cache and session backends are used; flush caches and sessions.

Clear pub/static/*, var/view_preprocessed/*. Deploy static content for all active locales/themes.

Access storefront checkout page (e.g., /de/checkout/ or /en/checkout/).

Observe checkout page fails to render (500 error) and an exception is logged with message:

Unable to unserialize value. Error: Syntax error
#1 Magento\Csp\Model\SubresourceIntegrityRepository->getData() called at …

Then flush all caches (or Redis cache DB) and re-open checkout — page works again.

Wait some time/daily usage or perform certain cache/asset operations → page fails again with the same error.



### Expected result

The checkout page should load normally and allow customers to proceed with orders regardless of cache flushes or SRI map regeneration.

The patch version should not introduce regression in CSP/SRI handling or cause checkout downtime.

### Actual result

Checkout page fails to display and returns a 500 error tied to Magento\Csp\Model\SubresourceIntegrityRepository.

Exception log shows “Unable to unserialize value. Error: Syntax error”.

Clearing caches and redeploying static contents temporarily resolves the problem, but the failure recurs later (after new cache entries or store usage).

Business impact: No orders processed while checkout is broken.

### Additional information


Observation: Works on staging (fresh install) but production fails after a few days.

Workaround: Rolling back to 2.4.7-p7 restores functionality permanently (so far).
