### Preconditions and environment

Magento version: 2.4.7-p8 (specifically patched state after applying p8 update)

PHP version: 8.3

Database: MySql 8.0.40

Cache/Session backend: Redis (separate system and session DBs)

Number of store views/locales: (e.g., 2 — de_DE and en_GB)

Deployment type: (Docker container, multi-web-node, full static content deploy)

Recent actions: Upgrade from 2.4.7-p7 to 2.4.7-p8, full static content deploy, then cache flush and Redis flush.


### Steps to reproduce

Upgrade Magento from 2.4.7-p7 to 2.4.7-p8 (apply patch, static content deploy for all locales/themes).

Ensure Redis cache and session backends are used; flush caches and sessions.

Clear pub/static/*, var/view_preprocessed/*. Deploy static content for all active locales/themes.

Access storefront checkout page (e.g., /de/checkout/ or /en/checkout/).

Observe checkout page fails to render (500 error) and an exception is logged with message:

Unable to unserialize value. Error: Syntax error
#1 Magento\Csp\Model\SubresourceIntegrityRepository->getData() called at …

Then flush all caches (or Redis cache DB) and re-open checkout — page works again.

Wait some time/daily usage or perform certain cache/asset operations → page fails again with the same error.



### Expected result

The checkout page should load normally and allow customers to proceed with orders regardless of cache flushes or SRI map regeneration.

The patch version should not introduce regression in CSP/SRI handling or cause checkout downtime.

### Actual result

Checkout page fails to display and returns a 500 error tied to Magento\Csp\Model\SubresourceIntegrityRepository.

Exception log shows “Unable to unserialize value. Error: Syntax error”.

Clearing caches and redeploying static contents temporarily resolves the problem, but the failure recurs later (after new cache entries or store usage).

Business impact: No orders processed while checkout is broken.

### Additional information


Observation: Works on staging (fresh install) but production fails after a few days.

Workaround: Rolling back to 2.4.7-p7 restores functionality permanently (so far).

title: SRI hashes stop checkout from loading static.js and mixins.js when bundling and minify is enabled
need_summary: Whether the checkout breakage from missing static.min.js and mixins.min.js under SRI-enabled bundling/minification is a real security-patch regression, with the answer anchored by the Adobe internal Jira AC-15867 and the official quality-patches commit b5333ad787f6946c2ac0452ede276a6f7a7c837d.
security_topic: checkout breakage from SRI hash generation with JS bundling/minification
question_text:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version 2.4.8-p3 
- CSP module enabled


### Steps to reproduce

1. Set store to production mode
2. Enable bundling and minify options for JS
3. Deploy the content
4. Add item to cart and browse to checkout
5. Check to see if static.min.js and mixins.min.js were loaded onto the page

### Expected result

The JS files are added to the <head> section and loaded on the page

### Actual result

Both of these files are missing from the page

### Additional information

It looks like the changes to Magento/Csp/Model/Deploy/Package/Processor/PostProcessor/Integrity.php in the recent patch to write all the integrity hashes to the file during deployment plus the new GenerateBundleAssetIntegrity.php are causing this. Mostly due to how it adds the files, it does not see the correct `.min.js` filename while writing the file and instead puts it as normal `.js` files.

Previously, the `sri-hashes.json` file would only contain the `requirejs-config.min.js` file hashes in it and nothing else. This led to the bundle files getting placed in the same group as everything else so the Config block that adds all the JS files in worked without issue since it could find the bundle file to add them after. 

Now, with the hashes, it correctly looks up the bundle file hashes because the plugin does a file search after deployment to get their correct names with .min.js in it and add their hashes causing them to be put in separate asset groups. It then fails to lookup the hashes for `static.min.js` and `mixins.min.js` because they are stored as `static.js` and `mixins.js` in the integrity map so it ends up trying to insert them into the existing js asset group but, since the bundle files aren't in there, fails to add them since it can't find the key to put them after.

The only way to make it work currently is either disable the minifying or bundling of the JS files.
answer_text:
I have created patch for this issue:
https://gist.github.com/hryvinskyi/3df14e684d67bd8f7d278f4340ab133b

**Update: This patch fixes both issues:**
Missing `static.min.js` and `mixins.min.js` when bundling and minification are enabled
Corrupted `sri-hashes.json` files caused by concurrent write race conditions

[c17] @magenizr 2025-10-21T20:49:28Z:
Hey folks,

Can we please discuss the quality of the patch? We have some concerns about its current design ( high-level ):

1. sri-hashes.json is being written to a static folder, which is read-only for most of us. ( https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.6-p13/app/code/Magento/Csp/Model/SubresourceIntegrity/Storage/File.php#L81 ) and ( https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.6-p13/app/code/Magento/Csp/Model/Deploy/Package/Processor/PostProcessor/Integrity.php#L86 )
2. sri-hashes.json contains up to 1.8 MB data. The file size depends on the number of assets (themes) and configured locales. For European merchants, it’s likely to be significantly larger.
```
[web@ssh-0 frontend]$ pwd
/var/www/html/codebase/pub/static/frontend
-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1.8M Oct 21 02:34 sri-hashes.json
```

3. The block `Magento/Csp/Block/Sri/Hashes.php` loads the entire file into memory via `checkout_index_index.xml` and `$integrityRepository->getAll()`

4. The file is being looped through and unserialized twice. ( https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.6-p13/app/code/Magento/Csp/Block/Sri/Hashes.php#L76-L90 )

**Suggestions:**

- Why not limit the file creation to locales (e.g. sri-hashes-en_US.json, sri-hashes-de_DE.json) and only unserialize the relevant file?
- Since the file can become quite large, wouldn’t it make sense to maintain it in a database instead?

comments.author: marshallthornton
comments.body:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version 2.4.8-p3 
- CSP module enabled


### Steps to reproduce

1. Set store to production mode
2. Enable bundling and minify options for JS
3. Deploy the content
4. Add item to cart and browse to checkout
5. Check to see if static.min.js and mixins.min.js were loaded onto the page

### Expected result

The JS files are added to the <head> section and loaded on the page

### Actual result

Both of these files are missing from the page

### Additional information

It looks like the changes to Magento/Csp/Model/Deploy/Package/Processor/PostProcessor/Integrity.php in the recent patch to write all the integrity hashes to the file during deployment plus the new GenerateBundleAssetIntegrity.php are causing this. Mostly due to how it adds the files, it does not see the correct `.min.js` filename while writing the file and instead puts it as normal `.js` files.

Previously, the `sri-hashes.json` file would only contain the `requirejs-config.min.js` file hashes in it and nothing else. This led to the bundle files getting placed in the same group as everything else so the Config block that adds all the JS files in worked without issue since it could find the bundle file to add them after. 

Now, with the hashes, it correctly looks up the bundle file hashes because the plugin does a file search after deployment to get their correct names with .min.js in it and add their hashes causing them to be put in separate asset groups. It then fails to lookup the hashes for `static.min.js` and `mixins.min.js` because they are stored as `static.js` and `mixins.js` in the integrity map so it ends up trying to insert them into the existing js asset group but, since the bundle files aren't in there, fails to add them since it can't find the key to put them after.

The only way to make it work currently is either disable the minifying or bundling of the JS files. 

### Release note

_No response_

### Triage and priority

- [ ] Severity: **S0** _- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [x] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S3** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S4** _- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”._

Same here on 2.4.6-p13. For us, the path `/var/www/html/codebase/pub/static/frontend/sri-hashes.json` isn’t an appropriate location to write such files.

```
[2025-10-20T06:16:32.327076+00:00] main.CRITICAL: Magento\Framework\Exception\FileSystemException: The path "/var/www/html/codebase/pub/static/frontend/sri-hashes.json" is not writable. in /var/www/html/codebase/vendor/magento/framework/Filesystem/Directory/Write.php:62
```

comments.author: magenizr
comments.body:
Hey folks,

Can we please discuss the quality of the patch? We have some concerns about its current design ( high-level ):

1. sri-hashes.json is being written to a static folder, which is read-only for most of us. ( https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.6-p13/app/code/Magento/Csp/Model/SubresourceIntegrity/Storage/File.php#L81 ) and ( https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.6-p13/app/code/Magento/Csp/Model/Deploy/Package/Processor/PostProcessor/Integrity.php#L86 )
2. sri-hashes.json contains up to 1.8 MB data. The file size depends on the number of assets (themes) and configured locales. For European merchants, it’s likely to be significantly larger.
```
[web@ssh-0 frontend]$ pwd
/var/www/html/codebase/pub/static/frontend
-rw-r--r--. 1 root root 1.8M Oct 21 02:34 sri-hashes.json
```

3. The block `Magento/Csp/Block/Sri/Hashes.php` loads the entire file into memory via `checkout_index_index.xml` and `$integrityRepository->getAll()`

4. The file is being looped through and unserialized twice. ( https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.6-p13/app/code/Magento/Csp/Block/Sri/Hashes.php#L76-L90 )

**Suggestions:**

- Why not limit the file creation to locales (e.g. sri-hashes-en_US.json, sri-hashes-de_DE.json) and only unserialize the relevant file?
- Since the file can become quite large, wouldn’t it make sense to maintain it in a database instead?

security_topic: performance impact of unconditional sales rule attribute loading
question_text:
If this issue is known or related to the recent upgrade, could you please advise if there is any temporary patch or workaround available until Magento officially releases a fix?

@senthilengg If you have patch or fix then kindly share it with us.
answer_text:
Hello @senthilengg, you make an excellent point. After deeper analysis, I agree this is a performance issue.

**The Problem:**
The plugin fires on **every** quote item collection load (line 262 in `Quote\Model\ResourceModel\Quote\Item\Collection.php`), not just during totals collection. This means:

1. Viewing cart page → Plugin fires → Queries `salesrule_product_attribute` table
2. For catalogs with 100k+ rows in this table, this adds unnecessary load time
3. These attributes are loaded even when they won't be used (no totals recalculation)

**Performance Impact:**
- Unnecessary DB query on every cart view
- Additional EAV attribute loading overhead  
- Scales poorly with number of rules × websites × customer groups × attributes

**Potential Solutions:**
1. **Lazy Load**: Only load salesrule attributes when `collectTotals()` is actually triggered
2. **Conditional Check**: Add flag to determine if rules need evaluation before loading attributes
3. **Caching**: Cache the active attributes per store/customer group to avoid repeated DB queries
4. **Move Loading Point**: Load attributes closer to rule validation in totals collection

Hence confirming the issue.

Thank you for bringing this issue to our attention. If you have a potential solution, we encourage you to submit a pull request. Your contributions significantly enhance Magento Open Source for everyone. Should you need any assistance, please don't hesitate to ask!

need_summary: Whether deleting a customer during registration must temporarily set isSecureArea to avoid the "Delete operation is forbidden for current area" failure, as described in the linked pull request magento/magento2#38462.

title: Public accessibility of cron.php causes errors and security concerns
need_summary: Whether Magento’s public `pub/cron.php` exposure should be treated as a security concern, anchored by the referenced `pub/.htaccess` rules in `https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/c8ff03033f9d79d9e6b6482086940153a28c6443/pub/.htaccess#L225-L234` and the maintainer’s confirmation that the web version of cron.php is not recommended.
security_topic: public access to cron.php and server-level blocking
question_text: cron.php should not be publicly accessible in a production environment.
answer_text:
You should have an entry in .htaccess (within pub folder) that prevents cron.php execution, like this:

https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/c8ff03033f9d79d9e6b6482086940153a28c6443/pub/.htaccess#L225-L234

Install Magento 2 2. Open a browser and navigate to https://yourdomain.com/cron.php. ### Expected result 1. cron.php should not be publicly accessible in a production environment. 2. Magento cron jobs should only run via CLI (bin/magento cron:run) and system cron tasks. ### Actual result 1. cron.php is exposed to the web by default. 2. comments.author: Gurdit
comments.body:
### Preconditions and environment

Magento / Adobe Commerce 2.4.8

### Steps to reproduce

1. Install Magento 2
2. Open a browser and navigate to https://yourdomain.com/cron.php.

### Expected result

1. cron.php should not be publicly accessible in a production environment.
2. Magento cron jobs should only run via CLI (bin/magento cron:run) and system cron tasks.

### Actual result

1. cron.php is exposed to the web by default.
2. If executed via HTTP, it can cause runtime errors, e.g.:
`TypeError: implode(): Argument #1 ($array) must be of type array, string given in /app/bvu7cj4frt2um/vendor/magento/module-cron/Observer/ProcessCronQueueObserver.php:967`

### Additional information

- cron.php exposure appears to be a legacy carryover from Magento 1, where web crons were common on shared hosting.
- Current Adobe Commerce documentation recommends system-level CLI cron only (bin/magento cron:run).
- Executing cron.php via HTTP can cause errors (e.g. implode(): Argument #1 ($array) must be of type array, string given) and may unnecessarily increase the attack surface.
- In modern deployments, cron.php is not required, but its presence in pub/ causes confusion about best practices.
- Clarification is needed whether this file should be considered deprecated or officially supported.

### Release note

_No response_

### Triage and priority

- [ ] Severity: **S0** _- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [x] Severity: **S3** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S4** _- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”._

comments.author: indykoning
comments.body:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version: 2.4.8-p2

### Steps to reproduce

1. Navigate to your magento store with a urlencoded non-utf8 character https://example.com/%C0, another example with a utf8 character but it being an emoj https://example.com/🔎
2. See as an error gets produced because invalid characters are put into the mysql query

### Expected result

A 404 page, or redirect if it has been set

### Actual result

An error gets thrown:
```
SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1271 Illegal mix of collations for operation ' IN ', query was: SELECT `url_rewrite`.* FROM `url_rewrite` WHERE (`request_path` IN ('%C0', '%C0/', '�', '�/')) AND (`store_id` IN ('1'))
```

### Additional information

This error comes from: vendor/magento/module-url-rewrite/Model/Storage/DbStorage.php@doFindOneByData

Changing the code like this, _does_ fix it. Question is, is it the **right** way?
```diff
-            $decodedRequestPath = urldecode($requestPath);
+            $decodedRequestPath = mb_convert_encoding(urldecode($requestPath), 'UTF-8');
```
This replaces those unknown characters to `?`

### Release note

_No response_

### Triage and priority

- [ ] Severity: **S0** _- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._

comments.author: DmitryFurs
comments.body:
@hostep @engcom-November @indykoning i was able to fix this by updating `app/etc/env.php`

For MariaDB 11.4

```patch
 'db' => [
     'table_prefix' => '',
     'connection' => [
         'default' => [
             'host' => 'localhost',
             'dbname' => 'magento_db',
             'username' => 'root',
             'password' => 'admin123',
             'model' => 'mysql4',
             'engine' => 'innodb',
-            'initStatements' => 'SET NAMES utf8;',
+            'initStatements' => 'SET NAMES utf8mb4;',
             'active' => '1'
         ]
     ]
 ]

```

For MySQL 8

```patch
 'db' => [
     'table_prefix' => '',
     'connection' => [
         'default' => [
             'host' => 'localhost',
             'dbname' => 'magento_db',
             'username' => 'root',
             'password' => 'admin123',
             'model' => 'mysql4',
             'engine' => 'innodb',
-            'initStatements' => 'SET NAMES utf8;',
+            'initStatements' => 'SET NAMES utf8mb4 COLLATE utf8mb4_general_ci;',
             'active' => '1'
         ]
     ]
 ]

```

Default value:
https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p3/setup/src/Magento/Setup/Model/ConfigOptionsList.php#L163

Documentation:
https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/configuration-guide/files/config-reference-envphp?utm_source=chatgpt.com#db

Hi everyone,

We investigated the reported issues in detail and, based on our findings, decided to revert the following commit for now: https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/a2e91ce36426696e3eb13ddae94fb1025795b867

During the RCA, we identified that the root cause is the default initStatement value (SET NAMES utf8). This setting was leading to the observed issues, including the URL rewrite problem.

As an immediate stabilization step, we have cleaned up the default initStatement value (SET NAMES utf8). This change has resolved the URL rewrite issue in our testing and is expected to prevent similar problems in other related scenarios as well.

We are now working on a more robust and comprehensive fix that addresses all these issues together, rather than applying partial or isolated changes. We'll share updates once the improved solution is ready for review.

Thanks to everyone for reporting, investigating, and collaborating on this. Your feedback has been very helpful.

title: Issue with Transaction Link Navigation Due to Incorrect parent_txn_id Handling (Related to Commit 48bdda9)
need_summary: Whether the admin transaction detail bug for refund/void links was already tracked in issue #39999, which the maintainer cited as the existing ticket and duplicate reference.
security_topic: admin transaction link navigation failure for refund/void transactions
question_text: When clicking on the Parent Transaction ID of a child transaction (refund or void), the admin panel should display the parent transaction details page.
answer_text:
Hello @Syamsg,

ISSUE #40165: Issue with Transaction Link Navigation Due to Incorrect parent_txn_id Handling (Related to Commit 48bdda9) Author: Syamsg Date: 2025-08-28T16:23:52Z Labels: Issue: ready for confirmation, Reported on 2.4.8 State: closed [c0] ### Preconditions and environment - Magento 2.4.8 (or affected version) installed with sample or real products. - Admin user account with full permissions. - Payment method configured to allow authorization, capture, refund, and void transactions. - At least one order placed and authorized successfully. ### Steps to reproduce - Log in to the Magento admin panel. - Navigate to Sales → Orders and open an existing order with a completed payment. - Click on the View Transactions link for the order. - Locate a child transaction (e.g., refund or void) in the list. - Click on the Parent Transaction ID link of that transaction. - Observe that the page redirects to an error page instead of displaying the parent transaction details. ### Expected result - When clicking on the Parent Transaction ID of a child transaction (refund or void), the admin panel should display the parent transaction details page. - All transaction information (txn ID, type, payment method, amount, status, etc.) should be visible correctly. - The page should not throw an error or redirect to an error page. ### Actual result - When clicking on the Parent Transaction ID of a refund or void transaction in the order transaction details, the admin panel redirects to an error page. - The parent transaction details are not displayed, and the user cannot view the transaction information. - Only standard payment transactions (authorization/capture) work correctly when clicking the parent transaction ID. ### Additional information The issue occurs in Magento core in vendor/magento/module-sales/Model/ResourceModel/Order/Payment/Transaction.php at line 153. Magento added the following condition in commit [48bdda9f93aa997e22e2ce8d7cfe63cea6d5756b]https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/48bdda9f93aa997e22e2ce8d7cfe63cea6d5756b `` if ($parentId && $txnType == 'authorization') { $transaction->setData('parent_id', $parentId); } `` Effect: Refund and void transactions have txn_type 'refund' or 'void', so parent_id is never set. In the admin panel, when opening Order → Transactions → Parent Transaction ID, the link tries to use: ``$this->_txn->getParentId()`` Since parent_id is null, this results in an error page. The transaction itself is correctly created and saved; the problem is only visible in the admin transaction detail UI. Example transaction data: Authorization transaction: ``{ "transaction_id": "44", "parent_id": null, "order_id": "141", "payment_id": "141", "txn_id": "250828171457084489", "parent_txn_id": null, "txn_type": "authorization", "is_closed": 1 }`` Capture transaction: ``{ "txn_id": "250828171457084489-capture", "payment_id": "141", "order_id": "141", "txn_type": "capture", "parent_txn_id": "250828171457084489", "transaction_id": "45", "parent_id": null }`` Observation: parent_txn_id exists for capture/refund/void, but parent_id remains null due to the condition. Admin block code uses: app\code\Magento\Sales\Block\Adminhtml\Transactions\Detail.php line 129 ``$this->getUrl('sales/transactions/view', ['txn_id' => $this->_txn->getParentId()])`` As parent_id is null, the URL is invalid, causing the error page. ### Release note Magento 2.4.8 – Admin transaction detail page fails when clicking Parent Transaction ID for refund or void transactions due to parent_id not being set. ### Triage and priority - [x] Severity: **S0** _- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._ - [x] Severity: **S3** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround._ - [ ] Severity: **S4** _- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”._ --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @m2-assistant 2025-08-28T16:23:55Z: Hi @Syamsg. title: Magento changed the entity type of $order after calls $invoice = $this->_invoiceService->prepareInvoice($order);
need_summary: Whether the order entity type mutation bug was fixed in AC-15401 and the answer rests on the AC-15401 commit b127bcbc9de24412589eb492a7a7b6b91d4ce77f and the stated target version 2.4.9-beta1.
security_topic: object state mutation during invoice preparation
question_text:
The $order object’s entity type changes to invoice after calling prepareInvoice().
$order should always remain of entity type "order".
answer_text:
Hello,

As I can see this issue got fixed in the scope of the internal Jira ticket AC-15401 by the internal team
Related commits:https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amagento%2Fmagento2+AC-15401&type=commits

Based on the Jira ticket, the target version is 2.4.9-beta1.

Thanks

Create a custom script or use a module with the following code: ```php /** @var \Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface $orderRepository */ /** @var \Magento\Sales\Model\Service\InvoiceService $invoiceService */ $orderId = 7030365; // use a valid order_id that can be invoiced $order = $orderRepository->get($orderId); $this->_logger->info("Before entity type: " . $order->getEntityType()); $invoice = $invoiceService->prepareInvoice($order); $this->_logger->info("After entity type: " . $order->getEntityType());` ``` 2. ### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version: 2.4.8-p2

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create a custom script or use a module with the following code:
```php
/** @var \Magento\Sales\Api\OrderRepositoryInterface $orderRepository */
/** @var \Magento\Sales\Model\Service\InvoiceService $invoiceService */

$orderId = 7030365; // use a valid order_id that can be invoiced
$order = $orderRepository->get($orderId);

$this->_logger->info("Before entity type: " . $order->getEntityType());
$invoice = $invoiceService->prepareInvoice($order);
$this->_logger->info("After entity type: " . $order->getEntityType());`
```
2. Run the custom script.



### Expected result
```php
Before entity type: order
After entity type: order
```
### Actual result
```php
Before entity type: order
After entity type: invoice
```
### Additional information

The $order object’s entity type changes to invoice after calling prepareInvoice().
$order should always remain of entity type "order".

**Impact:**
This behavior can cause unexpected side effects:
Other logic using the same $order object may incorrectly treat it as an invoice.
Leads to data integrity issues and inconsistent behavior.

comments.author: galdiuz
comments.body:
Technically the reason that this happens is because because the string is implicitly converted to an int when passed to [`$product->load($productId)`](https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/b28144ab99d6aae9f28ed10acdf615551cf6dba5/app/code/Magento/Catalog/Model/ProductRepository.php#L319), meaning `"123abc"` is converted to `123` per PHP's rules for [numeric strings](https://www.php.net/manual/en/language.types.numeric-strings.php). This means the product is successfully loaded but then cached with the proper ID in `$this->instancesById`, producing the error [on this line](https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/b28144ab99d6aae9f28ed10acdf615551cf6dba5/app/code/Magento/Catalog/Model/ProductRepository.php#L327) when attempting to access with `$productId` variable.

For the same reason `/catalog/product/view/id/123.0` or `/catalog/product/view/id/1.23e2` will produce the same error, as both these will be converted to the int `123`.

comments.author: Nuranto
comments.body:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version 2.4.8-p1
- PHP 8.3


### Steps to reproduce

1. Add a special character (multybyte) in postcode field
2. go to checkout to trigger a shipping estimatation

### Expected result

No error

### Actual result

```
SQLSTATE[HY000]: General error: 1271 Illegal mix of collations for operation 'in', query was:

SELECT main_table.tax_calculation_rate_id, main_table.tax_calculation_rule_id, main_table.customer_tax_class_id, main_table.product_tax_class_id, rule.priority, rule.position, rule.calculate_subtotal, rate.rate AS value, rate.tax_country_id, rate.tax_region_id, rate.tax_postcode, rate.tax_calculation_rate_id, rate.code, IF(title_table.value IS NULL, rate.code, title_table.value) AS title FROM tax_calculation AS main_table
 INNER JOIN tax_calculation_rule AS rule ON rule.tax_calculation_rule_id = main_table.tax_calculation_rule_id
 INNER JOIN tax_calculation_rate AS rate ON rate.tax_calculation_rate_id = main_table.tax_calculation_rate_id
 LEFT JOIN tax_calculation_rate_title AS title_table ON rate.tax_calculation_rate_id = title_table.tax_calculation_rate_id AND title_table.store_id = '1' WHERE (customer_tax_class_id = 3) AND (product_tax_class_id IN ('2')) AND (rate.tax_country_id = 'FR') AND (rate.tax_region_id IN(0, 0)) AND (rate.zip_is_range IS NULL) AND (rate.tax_postcode IS NULL OR rate.tax_postcode IN('*', '', '⠀', '⠀*', '�*', '�*')) ORDER BY priority ASC, tax_calculation_rule_id ASC, tax_country_id DESC, tax_region_id DESC, tax_postcode DESC, value DESC
```

### Additional information

Solution is in `src/vendor/magento/module-tax/Model/ResourceModel/Calculation.php::_createSearchPostCodeTemplates` : replacing string methods by their `mb_` equivalent solves the issue. I will create a PR asap.

### Release note

_No response_

title: Error. Could not save child: "Unknown entity type: Magento\Bundle\Model\Selection\Interceptor requested"
need_summary: Whether the bundle product save failure is caused by a plugin-induced interceptor lookup problem in Magento Bundle Selection, as explained by the EntityManager, MetadataPool, and TypeResolver behavior in the maintainer’s response.
security_topic: plugin-induced entity manager interceptor persistence failure
question_text:
Please also note that the specific methods created in the Vendor\Module\Plugin\MagentoFramework\Model\AbstractModel class seem to be irrelevant. No matter which method I create, the same error still occurs:
Could not save child: "Unknown entity type: Magento.Bundle.Model.Selection\Interceptor requested"
answer_text:
`Magento.Bundle.Model.Selection uses the EntityManager` instead of `AbstractDb` because it is not a simple row entity — it is a sub-entity of bundle products with complex multi-table persistence requirements and favours the Entity Manager for flexibility, metadata-driven persistence, and extensibility. This is why the class is registered in the MetadataPool `(app/code/Magento/Bundle/etc/di.xml)` and resolved by the EntityManager rather than a direct resource model save.

The root cause of the reported error is that when a plugin is applied to `Magento.Bundle.Model.Selection`, Magento generates an interceptor class (`Magento.Bundle.Model.Selection/Interceptor`). When `EntityManager::save()` is invoked, `TypeResolver::resolve()` is called with this interceptor class. Since TypeResolver does not have an explicit mapping for interceptors of concrete classes, the MetadataPool lookup fails and the system throws the Unknown entity type exception.

Other models are not affected because they either use traditional `AbstractDb::save()`, are accessed via interfaces (which already have interceptor mappings), or explicitly declare mappings in TypeResolver.

The better approach is to avoid plugging into `Magento.Bundle.Model.Selection` directly. Instead, target the corresponding resource model `(Magento.Bundle.Model.ResourceModel.Selection)` or rely on the appropriate API/data interfaces. This avoids persistence-level side effects and ensures forward compatibility with Magento’s architectural direction.

title: Cannot reindex all invalid on multi-thread indexers with active application lock
need_summary: Whether the multi-thread indexer lock bug can leave indexers stuck in an invalid/working state and the issue was fixed for internal Jira AC-15270 with target version 2.4.9-alpha3.
security_topic: indexer lock handling causing reindex failure
question_text: Cannot reindex all invalid on multi-thread indexers with active application lock
answer_text:
As I can see this issue got fixed in the scope of the internal Jira ticket AC-15270 by the internal team

Invalidate _catalog_category_product_ + _catalog_product_category_ indexers 2. Run `bin/magento cron:run --group index` to run **indexer_reindex_all_invalid** ### Expected result It should reindex properly ### Actual result > SQLSTATE[42S02]: Base table or view not found: 1146 Table 'magento2.catalog_category_product_index_store1_tmp' doesn't exist, query was: DELETE FROM `catalog_category_product_index_store1_tmp NB: this error is a bit misleading as the `catalog_category_product` indexer did reindex properly at first. ### Additional information After some analysis, here is what I found: When indexation starts, current indexer is locked (using a database lock by default). When multithreads are starting, parent connections are closed so we are losing the DB locks: https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p1/app/code/Magento/Indexer/Model/ProcessManager.php#L110 When indexation finishes, it checks if indexer is in a "working" state before to set it as "valid" https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p1/app/code/Magento/Indexer/Model/Indexer.php#L471 However, in State::getStatus() function, if status is "working" but NOT locked, then it returns "invalid" instead... https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p1/app/code/Magento/Indexer/Model/Indexer/State.php#L113 So it ends up keeping "working" state and not validating shared indexers (so catalog_product_category starts and the "Base table or view not found" appears). NB: this error is a bit misleading as the `catalog_category_product` indexer did reindex properly at first.

### Additional information

After some analysis, here is what I found:

When indexation starts, current indexer is locked (using a database lock by default).

When multithreads are starting, parent connections are closed so we are losing the DB locks:
https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p1/app/code/Magento/Indexer/Model/ProcessManager.php#L110

When indexation finishes, it checks if indexer is in a "working" state before to set it as "valid"
https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p1/app/code/Magento/Indexer/Model/Indexer.php#L471

However, in State::getStatus() function, if status is "working" but NOT locked, then it returns "invalid" instead...
https://github.com/magento/magento2/blob/2.4.8-p1/app/code/Magento/Indexer/Model/Indexer/State.php#L113

So it ends up keeping "working" state and not validating shared indexers (so catalog_product_category starts and the "Base table or view not found" appears).

The commit involved seems to be this one.
https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/d09224aba48e16d4c97c85bb66c1264d48be1a8e

_No response_

- [x] Severity: **S1** _- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._

title: Attribute Option Label Gets Overwritten When Updating Store Labels
need_summary: Whether partial updates to Magento attribute option store_labels were unintentionally overwriting other store-view labels, with the answer anchored by the internal Jira ticket AC-15208 and the target version 2.4.9-alpha3.
security_topic: store-label overwrite on partial attribute option update
question_text:
Magento’s implementation of the saveOption() method in \Magento\Eav\Model\Entity\Attribute\OptionManagement overwrites existing store-specific labels (store_labels) when an update is made, instead of merging the changes. As a result, labels for other store views are unintentionally removed when not explicitly included in the update payload.

### Expected result

- The store_labels for France should remain intact after the Germany label is updated.
- Magento should merge the provided labels with existing ones instead of fully overwriting them.
answer_text:

comments.body:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento 2.4.7-p6
- Product attribute with multiple store_labels (e.g., for France and Germany)
- Asynchronous or sequential update of attribute option using:
  `PUT /rest/all/async/bulk/V1/products/attributes/byAttributeCode/options/byOptionId`

- Magento’s implementation of the saveOption() method in \Magento\Eav\Model\Entity\Attribute\OptionManagement overwrites existing store-specific labels (store_labels) when an update is made, instead of merging the changes. As a result, labels for other store views are unintentionally removed when not explicitly included in the update payload.


### Steps to reproduce

1. Create or ensure a product attribute option has the following setup:

- option_id = 1234
- Labels:
       - Store ID 2 (France): "Bleu"
       - Store ID 3 (Germany): "Blau"

2. Call the API to update only the French label:
```
{
  "option_id": 1234,
  "store_labels": [
    {
      "store_id": 2,
      "label": "Bleu updated"
    }
  ]
}
```

3. Next call, update only the German label:
```
{
  "option_id": 1234,
  "store_labels": [
    {
      "store_id": 3,
      "label": "Blau updated"
    }
  ]
}
```
4. Observe that after the second update, the French label is removed (set to blank)       

### Expected result

- The store_labels for France should remain intact after the Germany label is updated.
- Magento should merge the provided labels with existing ones instead of fully overwriting them.


### Actual result

The second update overwrites the entire set of store_labels, removing any store-specific labels not included in the request.

### Additional information

The method \Magento\Eav\Model\Entity\Attribute\OptionManagement::saveOption() constructs a new options['value'][$optionId] array and replaces all existing labels. There is no merging logic, and missing labels are effectively erased.

Relevant code snippet:
`$options['value'][$optionId][0] = $optionLabel;
foreach ($option->getStoreLabels() as $label) {
    $options['value'][$optionId][$label->getStoreId()] = $label->getLabel();
}
`

### Release note

_No response_

- [ ] Severity: **S2** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround._
- [ ] Severity: **S3** _- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround._

title: Cache not invalidated after customer login — outdated content shown
need_summary: Whether the stale-cache behavior after customer login is fixed by PR #40008 and the related issue #40007 it references.
security_topic: cache invalidation after customer login exposing stale guest content
question_text:
### Preconditions and environment

Magento version: 2.4.8+ 
PHP version: 8.3
Full Page Cache: [built-in]

### Steps to reproduce

1. Enable all caches 
2. Navigate some pages
3. Login as a customer
4. Navigate previously visited pages



### Expected result

Dynamic elements related to the user’s state should be flushed from the cache (e.g., the header should only display the My Account dropdown).

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/6c4ab7be-d16c-4c4c-ba3c-e0dfdb85ba77)

### Actual result

These pages (except for the one the customer is redirected to) display elements for guests, such as the login/register links in the header.
PS: This problem becomes more important with custom content related to the logger user state.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f2b52d75-baed-4c93-b695-49ac3cb85ca8)

### Additional information

Maybe is related to this issue? 
https://github.com/magento/magento2/issues/40007
answer_text:
Anyway I applied a patch using[ this pull request ](https://github.com/magento/magento2/pull/40008)and it seems to fix this issue.
Once this PR is merged I think this issue can be considered closed.

title: Product Add to Cart issue in Rest API
need_summary: Whether the REST API allowed adding and ordering a product from the wrong website, which was confirmed as a bug and later fixed under internal Jira AC-15054 with target version 2.4.9-alpha3 and related commits.
security_topic: REST API cart bypass for website assignment restrictions
question_text:
### Preconditions and environment

- Magento version: 2.4.8-p1
- Multi website setup with MSI

### Steps to reproduce

1. Create Product and assigned it to any 1 website and multiple sources
2. Create empty cart using rest API in website where above product is not assined
3. Add above product in cart using rest API
4. Place order using rest API

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/ee1f4131-36bb-4851-897e-2185ace5c1ca)

### Expected result

It should be throw "Product that you are trying to add is not available." error.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/4ecf193f-af5d-47c8-912f-a4269151cdb1)

### Actual result

Able to add to cart product and place order even if it's not assigned to specific website.

![Image](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/634a52a6-8d3d-4b6a-b6ba-4eb8471378da)

### Additional information

Graphql add to cart mutation is throwing error so, only rest API have issue.
answer_text:
Hello,

As I can see this issue got fixed in the scope of the internal Jira ticket AC-15054 by the internal team
Related commits:https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amagento%2Fmagento2+spartans_pr_21082025_AC-15054&type=commits

Based on the Jira ticket, the target version is 2.4.9-alpha3.

Thanks

comments.author: maximus-sallam
comments.body:
> I have the same issue on magento 2.4.8 but unfortunatly I can not solve it by patching symphony modules.

Here's a temporary fix:
```
#!/bin/bash

# Define the path to the file
TARGET_FILE="./vendor/symfony/mailer/Transport/Smtp/Stream/SocketStream.php"

# Make sure the file exists before proceeding
if [ ! -f "$TARGET_FILE" ]; then
  echo "Error: File not found: $TARGET_FILE"
  exit 1
fi

# Create a backup
cp "$TARGET_FILE" "${TARGET_FILE}.bak"

# Patch the file
echo "Applying Patch..."
sed -i "s|\(\s*\)\$this->url = 'ssl://'\.\$this->url;|\1\$this->url = \$this->url;|" "$TARGET_FILE"
echo "Patch applied. Backup saved as ${TARGET_FILE}.bak"
echo
echo "Starting Database Schema Upgrade..."
php bin/magento setup:upgrade > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "Database Schema Upgrade Complete"
echo
echo "Starting compiler..."
php bin/magento setup:di:compile > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "Compilation Complete"
echo
echo "Starting Static Content Deployment..."
php bin/magento setup:static-content:deploy -f > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "Static Content Deployment Complete"
echo
echo "Starting Cache Flush..."
php bin/magento cache:flush > /dev/null 2>&1
echo "Cache Flush Complete"
```

title: Rest API: Call to a member function getVideoProvider() on null
need_summary: Whether the configurable-products children REST endpoint crashes when a child product has an external video, and the concrete fix anchor is the linked patch to Magento\Module\Configurable-Product\Model\LinkManagement.php that removes manual media_gallery_entries conversion and uses the child product's media gallery entries.
security_topic: REST API crash when configurable child has external video media
question_text:
Perform a call to `/index.php/rest/V1/configurable-products/<configsku>/children`
- Observe error in logs: `Call to a member function getVideoProvider() on null [] []`
answer_text:
We have attempted to reproduce the issue in the latest 2.4-develop instances by following the provided steps and preconditions. We are able to reproduce the issue. Please refer to the attached screenshot for details.

Steps to Reproduce:

- Create a configurable with a simple child product
- add a YouTube Video to the child product (other images not necessary)
- Video for your convenience: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=bSua9vMdrNM&t=18s
- Click Save, validate the video is there
- Generate oauth keys in integration
- Perform a call to /index.php/rest/V1/configurable-products/<configsku>/children
- Observe error in logs: Call to a member function getVideoProvider() on null [] []

comments.author: nrdevau
comments.body:
# Context
According to this article, Laminas MVC is retiring: https://getlaminas.org/blog/2025-06-06-laminas-mvc-is-retiring.html?trk=feed_main-feed-card_feed-article-content#content-how-to-migrate-from-laminas-mvc-to-mezzio

# Problem
The main concern we're wanting to address is determining what MVC solution Magento will use post PHP 8.5.

# Discussion
Some chatter from the community around this include:
https://www.linkedin.com/posts/trung-luu-09833232_laminas-project-laminas-mvc-is-retiring-activity-7341755577598910464-9xNW?utm_source=share&utm_medium=member_desktop&rcm=ACoAABGf_L4BCwByTcDebozZ-AnYnf6mphezrdc
https://magentocommeng.slack.com/archives/C4YS78WE6/p1750419803549029

Whether this impact is simply finding the few uses of `Laminas/Mvc` classes within the app (https://github.com/search?q=repo%3Amagento%2Fmagento2+%22Laminas%5CMvc%22&type=code) (thanks @sidolov) or whether we need to rethink how all model, view and controllers (the MVC part) are built and managed is a little unclear.

The usage of Laminas/Mvc is also around the bootstrapping of the application, so definitely a place that will have large impact regardless.

This issue is meant to aid in the community driven discussions that will happen alongside (before and probably after) the internal Adobe Magento decisions.

## Alternatives (already raised)
- Magento Framework implement the PSR-7, PSR-11 and PSR-15 specification
- Magento could fork and maintain Laminas/Mvc code in the meantime

### Additional Thoughts
- ~~Symfony controllers instead of Laminas ones? https://symfony.com/doc/current/controller.html~~
- Magento controllers are not extensions of Laminas ones, which is good. This means this issue probably won't force all future Module devs to implement some new way of building routes and so on
- Given that we have some pretty extensive testsuites built on core nowadays, we should be able to trial alternatives with confidence! (👍 for testing!)
- Would the [MFTF](https://github.com/magento/magento2-functional-testing-framework) tests need to updated (if they're currently used?)

There are definitely others better placed to direct this discussion, but hopefully this is a good starting place.

Excited to see how Adobe and the community collaborate and "think" together! :)

Cheers,
Nate

comments.author: cod43156
comments.body:
As part of ongoing modernization efforts, we would like to inform that the Laminas MVC framework, which is currently a key dependency in the Magento 2 Setup application, is being deprecated. To ensure long-term stability and alignment with modern PHP standards, we are actively evaluating alternatives to replace Laminas MVC in the Setup module.

The Laminas MVC framework is currently used in the following components:

> composer.json dependency list
> Magento\Setup\Application
> Magento\Setup\Module
> Magento\Setup\Mvc\Bootstrap\InitParamListener
> Magento\Setup\Mvc\View\Http\InjectTemplateListener
> Magento\Setup\Test\Unit\Mvc\Bootstrap\InitParamListenerTest

**Based on Analysis:**
The key constraint is that Setup runs before Magento is fully installed, so any replacement must be independent of Magento's core framework. We are considering three potential options to replace Laminas MVC, each with different benefits and migration impacts:

**1. Mezzio (Laminas Official Successor)**
 A modern middleware framework based on PSR standards and developed as the direct successor to Laminas MVC.

- Official Successor: Maintains architectural familiarity and compatibility with existing service configuration
- PSR-11, PSR-15, PSR-17 Compliant: Aligns with modern PHP-FIG recommendations
- Event & Routing Compatibility: Compatible event system and similar routing
- Migration Complexity: Moderate — will require adaptation of service manager and update of unit tests

**2. Symfony HTTP Foundation**
 Use Symfony components to build a custom setup application.

- Highly Flexible: Modular and widely adopted in the PHP ecosystem
- Performance Optimized: Robust and performant HTTP handling
- Migration Complexity: High — would require a complete rewrite of the Setup application flow and tests
- Learning Curve: Higher for teams unfamiliar with Symfony's architecture

**3. Slim Framework**
 A lightweight and efficient micro-framework with full PSR middleware support.

- Minimal & Fast: Great performance for limited-scope applications like setup
- PSR-7, PSR-11, PSR-15, PSR-17 Compliant: Fully standards-compliant
- Built-in Routing: Uses FastRoute for high-speed routing
- Migration Complexity: Moderate — will require updates to application flow and existing tests

**Community Feedback Request:**
We are seeking your input and recommendations on the direction we should take. Specifically:

- Do you have prior experience with any of the above frameworks in similar migration efforts?
- Are there other frameworks or approaches you believe we should consider?
- What concerns or blockers do you foresee with these proposed solutions?

Your expertise and insights are vital as we plan this important transition. Please share your thoughts in the discussion thread.

> **Note** **- Given that Mezzio is the official successor to Laminas MVC, it presents a logical and well-aligned choice for replacement.**

Thank you for your continued support!

comments.author: Vinai
comments.body:
Since the Laminas MVC package code is only used to initialize the service container and setup application initialization, implementing a lightweight replacement seems like a better option to me, compared to replacing one dependency with another.

I'd like to comment on some of the pros and cons listed above:

> PSR-11, PSR-15, PSR-17 Compliant: Aligns with modern PHP-FIG recommendations

Complying with these standards is hardly relevant, given the very limited part of Magento that is affected or would be using the new dependency.

> Highly Flexible: Modular and widely adopted in the PHP ecosystem

This again isn't very relevant, given the small scope of Magento that relies on Laminas MVC
Simplicity is a more attractive property in this circumstance.

> Official Successor: Maintains architectural familiarity and compatibility with existing service configuration
and
> Event & Routing Compatibility: Compatible event system and similar routing

Limiting the amount of work is great. Replacing Laminas MVC with Mezzio would pull in a large code base as a dependency, most of which isn't needed.

> Minimal & Fast: Great performance for limited-scope applications like setup
Speed is very important in general, even though it is hardly relevant here given it only would be used by the setup application.
The simplicity of Slim would be a good thing.

So, for what it's worth, my "recommendations" base on preference would be

1. Use the opportunity to remove the dependency and replace it with a specialized, small, and self-implemented service container and app initialization module.
2. If the choice is made to replace one external dependency with another, Mezzio would be my choice, give it makes migration less painful.
3. my third option would be Slim, because it's lightweight and relatively simple.
4. Symfony HTTP Foundation is overkill for what is needed.

comments.author: glo71317
comments.body:
First of all, thank you all for coming together and sharing your valuable inputs toward finalizing the approach to replace the **Laminas MVC framework**.

After considering feedback from both Adobe internal teams and the external Magento community, we’ve evaluated multiple options. While each approach has its own **pros** and **cons**, we are inclined to eliminate **Symfony HTTP Foundation** from the list due to several reasons.

**We are currently focusing on the following three approaches:**

**Custom Implementation:**
Remove the Laminas-MVC dependency entirely and replace it with a lightweight, self-implemented service container and application bootstrapper.

**Pros:** Minimal third-party dependencies, enhanced security, better long-term maintainability, and lower Composer bloat.
**Effort:** Higher initial effort but pays off long-term.

**Mezzio (Laminas successor):**
Replace Laminas-MVC with Mezzio, which is officially supported by Laminas.
**Pros:** Familiarity for existing Laminas users, relatively smoother migration.
**Effort:** Lower than custom implementation, but still requires moderate changes.

**Slim Framework:**
A minimal, lightweight alternative.
**Pros:** Easy to adopt, minimal code footprint.
**Cons:** Lacks some features we might require long-term; community support may be limited compared to Mezzio.

**Recommendation:**
**We believe Option 1** (custom lightweight implementation) is the most sustainable and secure path forward. It minimizes external dependencies, reduces attack surfaces, and ensures better control over the bootstrapping process for Adobe Commerce.
However, **Option 2 (Mezzio)** also remains a strong contender and should be prioritized in parallel consideration.

- It is the official successor to Laminas MVC
- Requires significantly less effort and time to migrate

We aim to finalize the preferred direction by end of this week (EOW) so that the team can begin implementation planning.
Your inputs are critical—please share any last thoughts or concerns so we can move forward confidently.

comments.author: glo71317
comments.body: @coffejhon Yes, After internal discussions, we have finalized Option 1 (custom lightweight implementation) as the most sustainable and secure path forward. This approach minimizes external dependencies while ensuring long-term maintainability and stability.

more info to reproduce
Steps to reproduce:
1. Delete any usles 3-d party Cli Class or make fatal PHP error
2. Run Cli command
3. Run Console cache:flush 
4. you will have error : 

Magento is broken and can't work anymore. Why ?
answer_text:
We attempted to reproduce the issue on the latest 2.4-develop branch, and we were able to encounter the same error message you reported. However, during our testing, we observed a few differences in behavior.

After running the setup:upgrade command, we initially encountered a different error related to a missing class. Once we proceeded to run the cache:flush command, the same error message you mentioned appeared, as shown in the screenshot below.

Steps we followed during testing:

bin/magento setup:upgrade

Then:

bin/magento cache:flush

This behavior seems consistent with your report — the CLI becomes unusable after a missing or invalid class is referenced during module setup or command registration.

ISSUE #40002: Special prices not displayed in 2.4.8 due to hasSpecialPrice() method change in final_price.phtml template Author: dstreit0106 Date: 2025-06-17T08:05:50Z Labels: Component: Catalog, Issue: Confirmed, Reproduced on 2.4.x, Priority: P2, Progress: done, Area: Pricing, Reported on 2.4.8 State: closed [c0] ### Preconditions and environment - Magento version: 2.4.8 - Upgrade path: Upgraded from Magento 2.4.6 or earlier - Environment: Any (development, staging, production) - Theme: Any theme using default Magento pricing templates - Product type: All product types with special prices configured - Special price configuration: Products with valid special prices set via Admin Panel > Catalog > Products > Advanced Pricing ### Steps to reproduce 1. Upgrade Magento installation from 2.4.6 (or earlier) to 2.4.8 1. Configure a simple product with a special price in Admin Panel: - Go to Catalog > Products - Edit any product - Click "Advanced Pricing" under Price field - Set a "Special Price" lower than the regular price - Save the product 1. View the product on category pages or product listing pages 1. Observe the price display ### Expected result - Special price should be displayed prominently - Regular price should be shown crossed out or with "Regular Price" label - Both prices should be visible to indicate the discount to customers ### Actual result - Only the regular price is displayed - Special price is not shown at all - No visual indication of any discount or special offer - The hasSpecialPrice() method returns false even when a valid special price exists ### Additional information Root cause analysis: The issue stems from changes made to the hasSpecialPrice() method in Magento 2.4.8. The method now uses a performance optimization with special*price*map for product listings, but this map is not properly initialized in many contexts, causing the method to return false even when products have valid special prices. Code location: - Affected template: vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/base/templates/product/price/final_price.phtml - Affected method: hasSpecialPrice() in pricing render blocks Temporary workaround: Replace the hasSpecialPrice() check in templates with direct price comparison: `// Instead of: if ($block->hasSpecialPrice()) $displayRegularPrice = $priceModel->getAmount()->getValue(); $displayFinalPrice = $finalPriceModel->getAmount()->getValue(); if ($displayFinalPrice < $displayRegularPrice)` Impact: - Critical business impact: Special prices/discounts not visible to customers - Affects sales and marketing strategies - Reduces conversion rates due to invisible promotions ### Release note Fixed: Special prices are now correctly displayed on product listing and category pages after the pricing performance optimization introduced in 2.4.8. The hasSpecialPrice() method now properly handles cases where the special*price*map is not initialized, ensuring consistent special price visibility across all store contexts. ### Triage and priority - [ ] Severity: **S0** *- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround.* - [ ] Severity: **S1** *- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround.* - [ ] Severity: **S2** *- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround.* - [ ] Severity: **S3** *- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround.* - [ > Severity: **S4** *- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”.* --- COMMENTS --- [c1] @m2-assistant 2025-06-17T08:05:53Z: Hi @dstreit0106.  - Only the regular price is displayed
 - Special price is not shown at all
 - No visual indication of any discount or special offer
 - The hasSpecialPrice() method returns false even when a valid special price exists

### Additional information

Root cause analysis:
The issue stems from changes made to the hasSpecialPrice() method in Magento 2.4.8. The method now uses a performance optimization with special*price*map for product listings, but this map is not properly initialized in many contexts, causing the method to return false even when products have valid special prices.

Code location:
 - Affected template: vendor/magento/module-catalog/view/base/templates/product/price/final_price.phtml
 - Affected method: hasSpecialPrice() in pricing render blocks

Temporary workaround:
Replace the hasSpecialPrice() check in templates with direct price comparison:
`// Instead of: if ($block->hasSpecialPrice())
$displayRegularPrice = $priceModel->getAmount()->getValue();
$displayFinalPrice = $finalPriceModel->getAmount()->getValue();
if ($displayFinalPrice < $displayRegularPrice)`

Impact:
 - Critical business impact: Special prices/discounts not visible to customers
 - Affects sales and marketing strategies
 - Reduces conversion rates due to invisible promotions

### Release note

Fixed: Special prices are now correctly displayed on product listing and category pages after the pricing performance optimization introduced in 2.4.8. The hasSpecialPrice() method now properly handles cases where the special*price*map is not initialized, ensuring consistent special price visibility across all store contexts.
### Triage and priority
 - [ ] Severity: **S0** *- Affects critical data or functionality and leaves users without workaround.*
 - [ ] Severity: **S1** *- Affects critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround.*
 - [ ] Severity: **S2** *- Affects non-critical data or functionality and forces users to employ a workaround.*
 - [ ] Severity: **S3** *- Affects non-critical data or functionality and does not force users to employ a workaround.*
 - [ > Severity: **S4** *- Affects aesthetics, professional look and feel, “quality” or “usability”.*

title: Font Size is not showing in TinyMCE editor in Magento 2.4.7-p5
need_summary: Whether the missing TinyMCE font-size control in Magento 2.4.7-p5 was removed by a recent security-patch TinyMCE upgrade, with the answer anchored by the linked Magento commits 38bf8dde3765131bc5c05b090457904602b10afb, 95b8deb8619da11bbe47c369319953981c2ca745, and 67fad326fb2e6bf571f578acec5cafa7cbe5d62d and the duplicate issue 39440.
security_topic: TinyMCE feature regression after security patch upgrade
question_text:
I've upgraded the production site on 2.4.7-p5 and endup on this issue that the font-size is not showing within a product configurations. 
For verification I have  installed the fresh vanilla instance for the similar version i.e 2.4.7-p5 and found the same issue on it.
answer_text:
Sounds like a duplicate of https://github.com/magento/magento2/issues/39440

TinyMCE was upgraded from version 5 to version 7 and then downgraded to version 6 in recent security patches, and it was an oversight that this option got removed by that TinyMCE upgrade.

You'd probably want to patch your installation with these changes, to add it back:
- https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/38bf8dde3765131bc5c05b090457904602b10afb
- https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/95b8deb8619da11bbe47c369319953981c2ca745
- https://github.com/magento/magento2/commit/67fad326fb2e6bf571f578acec5cafa7cbe5d62d

These are already included in Magento 2.4.8 / 2.4.8-p1, so upgrading to this version is also a way to fix this.

title: 2.4.4-p14
need_summary: Whether 2.4.4-p14 is unavailable because it is only for Adobe Commerce in Extended Support, and the answer points to Adobe’s lifecycle policy plus the APSB25-50 isolated patch for CVE-2025-47110.
security_topic: availability of a security patch and applicable update path for a Magento release
question_text:
One of my customers has the 2.4.4-pX version, and I want to update it to the latest patch.
I had no problem with the other version, but with this one, I saw that it is not published on GitHub, only the p13.

Does anyone know anything about this version? Why hasn't it been published yet?
answer_text:
I'm afraid you won't find 2.4.4-p14 for Magento Open Source, as that's only available for Adobe Commerce installations, since it's now in Extended Support.

See the documentation around that: https://experienceleague.adobe.com/en/docs/commerce-operations/release/planning/lifecycle-policy
> Extended support is available to Adobe Commerce customers only. It is not available for the Magento Open Source code base.

So I'd advise you to install the isolated security patch that got released: https://helpx.adobe.com/security/products/magento/apsb25-50.html#:~:text=Magento%20Open%20Source-,Isolated%20patch%20on%20CVE%2D2025%2D47110,-All and then try to find some time to update Magento to 2.4.8 so you're good for another couple of years.
